'''Danone''' ({{IPA|fr|danɔn}}) is a French [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] food-products corporation based in Paris. It was founded in 1919 in [[Barcelona]], Spain. It is listed on [[Euronext Paris]], where it is a component of the [[CAC 40]] stock market index. In 2020, Danone became the first listed company to adopt the status of ''société à mission'',<ref>{{cite web| title = Danone devient la première entreprise à mission du CAC40 | url = https://www.novethic.fr/actualite/entreprises-responsables/entreprise-responsable/isr-rse/danone-devient-la-premiere-entreprise-a-mission-du-cac40-et-salue-l-audace-de-ses-actionnaires-148721.html | website = Novethic| access-date = 17 June 2026}}</ref> as introduced by France's PACTE law of 2019.

Danone was formed through the 1973 merger of two French groups: Gervais Danone and Boussois-Souchon-Neuvesel (BSN). Gervais Danone itself resulted from the 1967 merger of Danone—founded by [[Isaac Carasso]] in Barcelona, Spain, in 1919—and Gervais. BSN was created in 1966 through the merger of the glass manufacturer Boussois and the glassworks company Souchon-Neuvesel. In 1994, the group adopted the name of its flagship fresh dairy brand, Danone. Under the leadership of Antoine Riboud, the company had become France's largest food manufacturer and the third-largest food group in Europe.

Over time the company organized its activities around three main business segments: fresh dairy and plant-based products, bottled water, and specialized nutrition, including medical and infant nutrition. Present in more than 120 markets in 2025, Danone reported sales of €27.283&nbsp;billion,<ref name="18Danone">{{cite web|url=https://www.danone.com/about-danone.html|title=About Danone – Danone|date=30 June 2026|website=Danone.com|access-date=30 June 2026}}</ref> making it the world's tenth-largest food company. The group employs approximately 90,000 people worldwide across more than 180 production sites.<ref>{{cite web| title = Danone en bref | url = https://www.danone.com/fr/groupe/qui-sommes-nous/danone-en-bref.html | website = Danone | access-date = 17 June 2026}}</ref>

In 2025 dairy and plant-based products represented 48% of total group sales; specialized nutrition (medical and infant), 34%; and water, 18%. Danone is the 4th largest dairy processing company globally, behind [[Nestlé]],<ref>{{cite web| title = Top 20 des laiteries dans le monde  | url = https://www.reussir.fr/lait/top-20-des-laiteries-dans-le-monde-des-chiffres-daffaires-record-en-2022 | website = Réussir Lait | access-date = 17 June 2026}}</ref> [[Dairy Farmers of America]], and [[Lactalis]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Top 20 des laiteries dans le monde | url = https://www.reussir.fr/lait/top-20-des-laiteries-dans-le-monde-des-chiffres-daffaires-record-en-2022 | website = Réussir Lait| access-date = 17 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Birth of Danone and creation of Gervais Danone (1919–1969) ===

[[File:Isaac carasso.jpg|thumb|150px|Isaac Carasso, founder of Danone]]
At the end of [[World War I]] in Europe, many children suffered from intestinal disorders linked to poor hygiene conditions.<ref>{{cite web | title = Hygiène et santé en Europe, fin XVIIIe siècle aux lendemains de la Première Guerre mondiale | url = https://hal.science/cel-01474846v1/document | website = HAL-SHS | date = 2017 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> [[Isaac Carasso]], a merchant, took an interest in the research of [[Élie Metchnikoff]], a researcher at the [[Pasteur Institute]] and [[Nobel laureate]] in 1908. This research focused on the benefits of [[Yogurt|yoghurts]] and lactic [[ferments]] on health, highlighting in particular their use in treating intestinal disorders. Isaac Carasso was already familiar with the virtues of : in [[Thessaloniki]], where he was from, the product was widely available and sold in the streets by the kilogram. He decided to introduce it in Spain, incorporating lactic cultures on the advice of doctors. The [[Pasteur Institute]] supplied the cultures.

In 1919 in a small workshop in [[Barcelona]], Isaac Carasso launched yoghurt production.<ref>{{cite web | title = Le yaourt a 100 ans : comment Danone s'adapte un siècle plus tard | url = https://www.leparisien.fr/economie/consommation/le-yaourt-a-100-ans-comment-danone-s-adapte-un-siecle-plus-tard-17-11-2019-8195157.php | website = Le Parisien | date = 17 November 2019 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> The yoghurts were made with fresh milk and delivered the following day. The brand was initially called "Danon", after the Catalan nickname of his son "petit Daniel".<ref name="Pourquoi Danone s'appelle Danone">{{cite web | title = Pourquoi Danone s'appelle Danone ? | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2009/07/30/04015-20090730ARTFIG00198-pourquoi-danone-s-appelle-danone-.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 30 July 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Daniel Carasso, fondateur de Danone | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/disparitions/article/2009/05/23/daniel-carasso-fondateur-de-danone_1197142_3382.html | website = Le Monde | date = 23 May 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> However, a proper name could not serve as a trade name under [[Spanish law]]. The founder added an "e" to register the brand, which became "Danone". In 1923, the Barcelona College of Physicians officially recognized the properties of yoghurt. The pots were sold in [[pharmacies]] on doctors' recommendations, and later in dairy shops.

After commercial studies in [[Marseille]] and a [[bacteriology]] placement at the [[Institut Pasteur]], [[Daniel Carasso]], then aged 20, launched the brand in France in 1929 by founding the Société Parisienne du yoghourt Danone. The first factory opened in 1932 in [[Levallois-Perret]]. The company progressively developed its distribution network in the Paris region, contributing to the spread of yoghurt into everyday consumption. The product range expanded rapidly. In 1937, Dany, the first fruit yoghurt, was launched. Fruit-flavored yoghurts were commercialized in 1953, smooth-style yoghurts in 1963, and gelled varieties in 1966.<ref>{{cite web | title = Le fondateur de Danone s'éteint à 103 ans | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2009/05/18/04015-20090518ARTFIG00498-le-fondateur-de-danone-s-eteint-a-103-ans-.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 18 May 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

In 1942 the [[Military occupation|occupation]] of France forced Daniel Carasso to take refuge in the United States. He continued developing the brand, acquired a yoghurt<ref>{{cite web | title = Daniel Carasso, 103, Dies; Helped Make Yogurt Popular | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2009/05/21/business/21carasso.html | website = The New York Times | date = 21 May 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> manufacturer, and launched Dannon Milk Products. On the advice of French publicist [[Raymond Loewy]], the brand's [[spelling]] was Americanized to avoid mispronunciation.<ref name="Pourquoi Danone s'appelle Danone"/> Dannon Inc. was incorporated in the United States.

Back in France, Daniel Carasso sold his American company to [[Beatrice Foods]] (it would be repurchased by Danone France in 1981) and sought to strengthen Danone. The company merged in 1967 with Fromageries {{Interlanguage link|Gervais (company)|lt=Gervais|fr|Gervais (entreprise)}} to form Gervais-Danone.

=== From yoghurt to its jar (1970–1977) ===

[[File:Danone factory in Bierun.JPG|thumb|left|Danone's factory in Bieruń, Poland]]

In the early 1970s Gervais-Danone acquired numerous pasta and canned food brands: Milliat Frères, [[Panzani]], Garbit, Petitjean, and Lhuissier, thereby becoming the leading pasta producer in France.

At the same time [[Boussois-Souchon-Neuvesel]] (BSN), initially present in the [[packaging]] market, saw its attempted takeover of glassmaker [[Saint-Gobain]] fail. Its chairman Antoine Riboud decided to reorient the company's strategy by diversifying into the food industry, with the objective of moving from packaging production to food products. BSN took control of the [[Évian]] and [[Badoit]] bottled mineral water brands, Blédina, and the Kanterbräu and [[Kronenbourg]]<ref name="lefigaro.fr">{{cite web | title = Pourquoi Danone s'appelle Danone | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2009/07/30/04015-20090730ARTFIG00198-pourquoi-danone-s-appelle-danone-.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 30 July 2009 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> breweries, becoming a major player in the beer, mineral water, and infant nutrition sectors.

In 1973 BSN merged with Gervais Danone. The new entity was named BSN-Gervais-Danone.<ref name="lesechos.fr">{{cite web | title = Danone se retourne sur ses origines | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/2009/07/danone-se-retourne-sur-ses-origines-474797 | website = Les Échos | date = 2009 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> The group's main activities at that point were fresh products, [[beverages]], pasta, and prepared<ref>{{cite web | title = B.S.N.-Gervais-Danone prend le contrôle de Frigécrème | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/1980/02/13/b-s-n-gervais-danone-prend-le-controle-de-frigecreme_2813312_1819218.html | website = Le Monde | date = 13 February 1980 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> meals. Antoine Riboud, who initiated the operation, took over its leadership.

=== Refocusing on food, diversification and group expansion (1978–1995) ===

In 1978 BSN-Gervais Danone acquired the Belgian brewery [[Alken-Maes|Alken]]. The following year, in the wake of the oil crisis, the company divested its flat glass activities and refocused on food. The group expanded and extended its activities across Europe.<ref name="lesechos.fr"/> In 1980, it acquired the food branch of [[Générale Occidentale]], specializing in grocery and confectionery, and owner of numerous brands including [[Carambar]], [[Liebig]], [[Vandamme]], [[La Pie qui Chante]], and [[Maille (company)|Maille]]. BSN-Gervais Danone became France's leading food company.

In 1983 the group dropped the BSN-Gervais Danone name and simplified it to BSN.<ref name="Unilever et BSN se partagent Ortiz">{{cite web | title = Unilever et BSN se partagent Ortiz-Miko | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/1993/12/unilever-et-bsn-se-partagent-ortiz-miko-917479 | website = Les Échos | date = 1993 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> Despite this change, the fresh dairy products inherited from Gervais Danone remained a core activity.<ref name="lefigaro.fr"/>

In 1987 BSN entered the biscuit market by acquiring Générale Biscuit, owner of the [[LU (biscuits)|LU]] brand and present in several European countries. Two years later, the group acquired several European subsidiaries of the American company [[Nabisco]], including [[Belin]]. It thereby became the leading biscuit producer in Europe and one of the principal global players.<ref name="nouvelobs.com">{{cite web | title = Danone : de la verrerie à l'alimentaire | url = https://www.nouvelobs.com/economie/20070709.OBS5789/danone-de-la-verrerie-a-l-alimentaire.html | website = Nouvel Obs | date = 9 July 2007 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> The group's turnover at that time stood at 48.7&nbsp;billion francs.

In 1993 BSN acquired Vivagel<ref name="Unilever et BSN se partagent Ortiz"/> and combined its food activities with those of the {{ill|Saint Louis Sucre|lt=Saint Louis Group|fr|Saint Louis Sucre}} group (Marie, [[William Saurin (French food company)|William Saurin]], La Belle Chaurienne) within a joint subsidiary named Panzalim. Following Saint-Louis's withdrawal in 1996, BSN recovered its full portfolio of brands.

As its international presence grew, the BSN name remained little-known to the general public – particularly as it was already used by a bank in Spain, a textile company in the United States, and a [[television channel]] in Japan. In a context of [[globalization]], the group chose to leverage its most visible brand, Danone, which alone accounted for a quarter of turnover. In 1994, BSN changed its name to "Groupe Danone", represented by "the child with a star". The company at that point owned nearly 300 brands.<ref name="nouvelobs.com"/>

=== Refocusing on three areas and the beginning of internationalization (1996–2006) ===

[[File:FranckRiboudMEDEF2008.jpg|thumb|Franck Riboud, CEO of Danone from 1996 to 2014 and chairman of the board from 2014 to 2017, then honorary chairman since 2017.]]

Franck Riboud, CEO of Danone from 1996 to 2014, chairman of the board of directors from 2014 to 2017, and honorary chairman since 2017.

In 1996 Antoine Riboud, chairman of the Danone group, retired at the age of 77 and stepped down from his position. His son Franck succeeded him. This year marked the beginning of a period of refocusing for the company around health and healthy [[eating]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Portrait : Franck Riboud, Tintin au pays des yaourts | url = https://www.nouvelobs.com/economie/20120214.OBS1398/portrait-franck-riboud-tintin-au-pays-des-yaourts.html | website = Nouvel Obs | date = 14 February 2012 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> and an acceleration of its international development.

Following several acquisitions in [[emerging markets]], the Danone group acquired 51% of [[Hangzhou Wahaha Group]], the leading non-alcoholic beverage producer in China. [[Zong Qinghou]], the company's founder, became chairman of Danone-Wahaha, which held nearly 39 joint ventures.<ref>{{cite web | title = Conflit avec Wahaha : Danone encore débouté | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/conflit-avec-wahaha-danone-encore-deboute.N25337 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 2007 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> All products were marketed under the Wahaha brand. Through this partnership, the Danone group generated three-quarters of its Chinese activity and 10% of its global sales.

In the years that followed, the company divested more than half of its grocery activities and all of its confectionery: [[Panzani]], [[Amora (mustard)|Amora Maille]], and [[William Saurin (French food company)|William Saurin]] were sold to [[Paribas Affaires Industrielles]]; Marie to [[Uniq plc]]; [[Liebig's Extract of Meat Company|Liebig]] to [[Campbell's]];<ref>{{cite web | title = Paribas multiplie les rachats dans l'agroalimentaire | url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/paribas-multiplie-les-rachats-dans-l-agroalimentaire,23990 | website = LSA | date = 2000 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> and [[La Pie qui Chante]], [[Carambar]], and Vandamme to [[Cadbury]].<ref>{{cite web | title = La Pie qui Chante | url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/produits/la-pie-qui-chante,133803 | website = LSA | date = 2009 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref>

At the same time the company accelerated its [[internationalization]] strategy in [[emerging markets]] and listed on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite web | title = Franck Riboud | url = https://www.journaldunet.com/economie/magazine/1034971-la-longevite-des-dirigeants-du-cac-40/1034980-franck-riboud | website = Journal du Net | date = 1998 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> That same year, the group was the official supplier of dairy products at the [[FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web | title = La Coupe du monde 1998 est pleine de partenaires officiels | url = https://www.liberation.fr/sports/1996/09/20/la-coupe-du-monde-1998-est-pleine-de-partenaires-officielshier-danone-a-rejoint-la-poste-hewlett-pac_181754/ | website = Libération | date = 20 September 1996 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> Three brands were highlighted: Danone, [[Évian]], and [[LU (biscuits)|LU]]. In 1999, the group divested its packaging and beer operations, including the sale of [[Kronenbourg]] and Alken-Maes breweries to [[Scottish & Newcastle]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web | title = Archives – Le Soir | url = https://www.lesoir.be/archives/recherche | website = Le Soir | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref> That same year, Danone chose to establish a research and development center in [[Palaiseau]], in the [[Paris-Saclay]] scientific and technology cluster.<ref>{{cite web | title = La recherche de Danone s'installe à Palaiseau | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/archives/article/2000/09/13/la-recherche-de-danone-s-installe-agrave-palaiseau_94672_1819218.html | website = Le Monde | date = 13 September 2000 | access-date = 26 June 2026}}</ref>

In the years that followed, Danone continued its development in emerging markets, notably in Latin America (Uruguay, Chile), Asia (China, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, and Vietnam), North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Egypt), and the Middle East (Israel, Saudi Arabia), as well as in North America with the acquisition of Stonyfield Farm, a global leader in organic yoghurt.<ref>{{cite web | title = Company News; Group Danone Increases Stake in Stonyfield Farm to 80% | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/13/business/company-news-group-danone-increases-stake-in-stonyfield-farm-to-80.html | website = The New York Times | date = 13 January 2004 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

On 10 January 2001 the newspaper [[Le Monde]] revealed the forthcoming closure of two [[LU (biscuits)|LU]] factories. On 29 March, Danone announced the reorganization of its biscuit operations in Europe, aimed at rationalizing industrial capacity. The plan provided in particular for the closure of two LU factories in France, in Calais and Ris-Orangis, as well as the elimination of 1,780 jobs across Europe, including 570 in France. This decision provoked significant social and political mobilization in France, even as the company was profitable. Strikes, demonstrations, and calls to boycott Danone products were organized, relayed by certain elected officials, trade unions, and associations. The movement attracted considerable public attention, though it also generated divisions. The affair gave rise to a notable media controversy in spring 2001, affecting the group's image. It was also accompanied by legal proceedings related to the creation of critical websites against Danone: after an initial conviction, a court of appeal reaffirmed in 2003 the primacy of freedom of expression in this context.

Antoine Riboud died on 5 May 2002, aged 83.<ref>{{cite web | title = Antoine Riboud : la mort d'un grand patron visionnaire | url = https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2002/05/06/402241-antoine-riboud-la-mort-d-un-grand-patron-visionnaire.html | website = La Dépêche | date = 6 May 2002 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

[[File:Danone Saclay.JPG|thumb|The Danone [[Research and development|R&D]] center in [[Palaiseau]] ([[Paris-Saclay]]).]]

In July 2005 a rumor spread about a possible hostile takeover of Danone by [[PepsiCo]]. The story, broken by ''Challenges'' magazine, claimed that PepsiCo had acquired 3% of Danone's capital. Politicians from both left and right, as well as trade unions, rallied to defend the Danone group, describing it as "an industrial jewel". Pepsi denied any such intention, but the affair caused a significant stir, and the [[French government]] announced it would do everything possible to protect the Danone group. The [[Financial Markets Authority]] (AMF) announced that PepsiCo had certified on 24 July that it was not preparing a bid for the group.<ref>{{cite web | title = PepsiCo a certifié à l'AMF ne pas préparer une opération sur Danone | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/2005/07/pepsico-a-certifie-a-lamf-ne-pas-preparer-une-operation-sur-danone-612736 | website = Les Échos | date = 25 July 2005 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

At the same time Danone found that alongside the 39 [[joint-venture]] structures, some sixty factories and [[Food distribution|distribution]] companies were producing and selling beverages illegally under the Wahaha brand. The French group accused its Chinese partner of failing to respect the [[non-compete clauses]]. It then attempted to take control of these subsidiaries, but was rebuffed by [[Zong Qinghou]], who denounced the intrusion of foreign companies in China.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone découvre le supplice chinois de l'investisseur | url = https://www.nouvelobs.com/rue89/rue89-monde/20070614.RUE0659/danone-decouvre-le-supplice-chinois-de-l-investisseur.html | website = Nouvel Obs | date = 14 June 2007 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> Wahaha alleged that the French company was aware of the situation and accused it of seeking too large a share in the joint ventures.<ref>{{cite web | title = Fin de conflit entre Danone et le chinois Wahaha | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/fin-de-conflit-entre-danone-et-le-chinois-wahaha.N118256 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 30 September 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> Danone entered into [[negotiations]] and then took the matter to court in 2007. French President [[Nicolas Sarkozy]] even raised the case with Chinese President [[Hu Jintao]] during an official visit.<ref>{{cite web | title = Première fortune de Chine : Zong Qinghou, l'ennemi de Danone | url = https://www.nouvelobs.com/rue89/rue89-economie/20101028.RUE9196/premiere-fortune-de-chine-zong-qinghou-l-ennemi-de-danone.html | website = Nouvel Obs | date = 28 October 2010 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> In 2009, an amicable agreement was reached between the two parties. The Danone group exited the joint venture and sold its shares to its former partner. Following this separation, Danone left the non-alcoholic beverage market in China.

In 2006 Franck Riboud refocused Danone's activities on its three most promising businesses: fresh dairy products, bottled [[mineral water]], and [[biscuits]]. These three sectors alone represented 85% of sales.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone se retourne sur ses origines | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/2009/07/danone-se-retourne-sur-ses-origines-474797 | website = Les Échos | date = 6 July 2009 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Continued internationalization around dairy products, water, and infant nutrition (2007–2019) ===

In 2007 Danone refocused once again and divested its biscuit activity<ref>{{cite web | title = Franck Riboud | url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/annuaire-professionnels-grande-consommation/riboud-franck/121622 | website = LSA | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> — which included the [[TUC (cracker)|Tuc]], [[Belin]], and [[LU (biscuits)|LU]] brands – selling it to [[Kraft]] (subsequently renamed [[Mondelēz International]]). 7 July marked the end of the cooperation between Eden and Danone around the Château d'eau business.

Having divested all of the LU assets, the group launched a takeover bid for the Dutch company [[Numico]] on 8 July.

Danone thus acquired one of the global leaders in infant nutrition and medical nutrition. The transaction was completed for €12.3&nbsp;billion. On 29 October, the Danone board of directors approved the sale of its Biscuits and cereal products division to [[Kraft Foods]] for €6.3&nbsp;billion. From that point on, the company organized itself around four activities: fresh dairy products, water, infant nutrition, and medical nutrition.

[[Daniel Carasso]], then honorary chairman of the company, died on 17 May 2009 at the age of 103.<ref name="Pourquoi Danone s'appelle Danone"/>

On 18 June 2010 Danone partnered with [[Unimilk]], one of Russia's leading milk producers. Together, they merged their fresh dairy product activities in Russia, [[Ukraine]], [[Kazakhstan]], and [[Belarus]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Les revenus de Danone portés par le russe Unimilk | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2011/04/14/04015-20110414ARTFIG00449-les-revenus-de-danone-portes-par-le-russe-unimilk.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 14 April 2011 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> This joint venture gave rise to the number one dairy products company in that region.<ref name="Danone se renforce à l'étranger">{{cite web | title = Danone se renforce à l'étranger | url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/danone-se-renforce-a-l-etranger,114667 | website = LSA | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> Russia became the fifth most important market for the French company.

In 2010 the group also acquired Immédia, the third-largest [[smoothie]] producer in France, as well as the American company Medical Nutrition.<ref name="Danone se renforce à l'étranger"/> With its $16&nbsp;million in [[Sales turnover|turnover]], Medical Nutrition joined Danone's nutrition division, which that same year generated $70&nbsp;million in North America.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone acquiert Medical Nutrition | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2010/06/11/04015-20100611ARTFIG00448-danone-acquiert-medical-nutrition.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 11 June 2010 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> The objective was to strengthen Danone's position in health products and medical nutrition in particular, a fast-growing market.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone se renforce sur le marché des boissons fruitées | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2010/08/24/04015-20100824ARTFIG00358-danone-se-renforce-sur-le-marche-des-boissons-fruitees.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 24 August 2010 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> In April 2012, Danone was a candidate to acquire Pfizer's infant nutrition business, but that activity was ultimately sold to [[Nestlé]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone déçu de l'échec du rachat de l'alimentation infantile de Pfizer | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/danone-decu-de-l-echec-du-rachat-de-l-alimentation-infantile-de-pfizer.N173649 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 26 April 2012 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> Like medical nutrition, infant nutrition was growing strongly in [[emerging markets]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone : un bébé trop goulu | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2012/04/24/danone-un-bebe-trop-goulu_1690472_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 24 April 2012 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

[[File:Publicité Yaourt Danone Corniche Casablanca Maroc.jpg|alt=Casablanca advertisement|left|thumb|"Double zéro" advertisement on the Casablanca corniche in November 2024]]

In 2011 the share of sales achieved in emerging markets crossed a milestone, reaching 51%.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone performe en 2011 grâce aux pays émergents | url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/danone-performe-en-2011-grace-aux-pays-emergents,127949 | website = LSA | date = 2012 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> 

In June 2012 the group announced that it was raising its stake in Centrale Laitière, the Moroccan leader in dairy products – with whom Danone had worked since 1953 – to 67%.

In October 2012 Danone partnered with the Abraaj investment fund to acquire 49% of Fan Milk, a company that manufactures and distributes frozen dairy products and juices in [[Ghana]], [[Nigeria]], [[Togo]], [[Burkina Faso]], [[Benin]], and [[Ivory Coast]].

On 18 July 2014 Danone announced the acquisition of 40% of the capital of the Kenyan group Brookside, the leading dairy products group in East Africa.

On 20 May 2013 Danone announced a 4.0% strategic stake in [[Mengniu]], the number one dairy products company in China, through an agreement with COFCO (China's leading state-owned food company and principal shareholder of Mengniu). In February 2014, Danone announced that it had raised its stake in Mengniu from 4.0% to 9.9%, for €486&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone raises stake in China Mengniu Dairy | url = https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/02/12/us-mengniu-danone-idUSBREA1B04C20140212/ | website = Reuters | date = 12 February 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> Danone became the company's second largest shareholder. In parallel, in May 2013, a joint venture was created between Danone and Mengniu to develop the fresh dairy product category.

In August 2013 a false alert<ref>{{cite web | title = Fonterra condamné à dédommager Danone dans la fausse affaire du lait contaminé | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/fonterra-condamne-a-dedommager-danone-dans-la-fausse-affaire-du-lait-contamine.N621718 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 8 December 2017 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> regarding the toxicity of ingredients in infant milks sold in Asia created a climate of panic.

In February 2014 Danone mandated investment bank [[JPMorgan Chase|JP Morgan]] with a view to divesting its medical nutrition division, valued at approximately €3&nbsp;billion,<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone prêt à vendre sa nutrition médicale | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/2014/02/13/20005-20140213ARTFIG00103-danone-pret-a-vendre-sa-nutrition-medicale.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 13 February 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Danone considers sale of medical nutrition unit | url = https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/02/12/us-danone-medicalnutrition-idUSBREA1B1T720140212/ | website = Reuters | date = 12 February 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref> before reaffirming its four core businesses (Fresh Dairy Products, Water, Infant Nutrition, and Medical Nutrition) in December 2014.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone renonce à vendre sa division nutrition médicale | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2014/12/12/danone-renonce-a-vendre-sa-division-nutrition-medicale_4539412_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 12 December 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

On 1 October 2014 [[Franck Riboud]] handed over the general management of the company to [[Emmanuel Faber]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Le PDG de Danone Franck Riboud passe la main | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-eco/2014/09/02/97002-20140902FILWWW00264-le-pdg-de-danone-franck-riboud-passe-la-main.php | website = Le Figaro | date = 2 September 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

On 31 October 2014 Danone, Mengniu, and Yashili announced that they had signed an agreement under which Danone participated in a reserved capital increase of the Chinese company Yashili for an amount of €437&nbsp;million. Danone then held 25.0% of Yashili's capital.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone to buy stake in Yashili | url = https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/10/31/us-yashili-danone-m-a-idUSKBN0IK02Y20141031/ | website = Reuters | date = 31 October 2014 | access-date = 23 June 2026}}</ref>

In November 2015 Danone announced that it had concluded a definitive agreement with the Chinese group Yashili and its parent company [[Mengniu]] for the sale of the Dumex infant nutrition brand, for a price of €150&nbsp;million. Dumex's sales in China had been significantly below their early 2013 levels, and the brand had been subject to a value write-down of €398&nbsp;million.

In June 2016 Danone announced the acquisition of a 40% stake in [[Michel et Augustin]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone prend le contrôle de Michel et Augustin | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2016/06/28/danone-prend-le-controle-de-michel-et-augustin_4960019_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 28 June 2016 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In July 2016, Danone announced the acquisition of WhiteWave Foods<ref>{{cite web | title = Les cinq raisons du rachat de WhiteWave par Danone | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/les-cinq-raisons-du-rachat-de-whitewave-par-danone.N401712 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 7 July 2016 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> for $12.5&nbsp;billion including assumed debt. This American company, specializing in organic dairy products and plant-based products, owns the Horizon Organic, Silk, and Earthbound Farm brands. In April 2017, to obtain competition authority clearance for the WhiteWave acquisition, Danone announced the sale of Stonyfield.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone promet une cession pour boucler l'achat de l'américain WhiteWave | url = https://www.latribune.fr/entreprises-finance/industrie/agroalimentaire-biens-de-consommation-luxe/danone-promet-une-cession-pour-boucler-l-achat-de-l-americain-whitewave-675649.html | website = La Tribune | date = 3 April 2017 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In July 2017, Danone sold Stonyfield to [[Lactalis]] for $875&nbsp;million (€768&nbsp;million), to comply with requirements from US competition authorities.

In February 2018 Danone sold a 14% stake in Yakult for €1.5&nbsp;billion, retaining only a 7% interest.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone to sell $1.9 billion Yakult stake in quest to boost shareholder returns | url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-danone-yakult/danone-to-sell-1-9-billion-yakult-stake-in-quest-to-boost-shareholder-returns-idUSKCN1FY0OR/ | website = Reuters | date = 14 February 2018 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In April 2019 Danone announced the sale of Earthbound Farm, an American brand specializing in organic salads, to Taylor Farms.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone sells U.S. organic salad business to Taylor Farms | url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-danone-earthbound/danone-sells-u-s-organic-salad-business-to-taylor-farms-idUSKCN1RO0F8/ | website = Reuters | date = 12 April 2019 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In October 2020 Danone announced the sale of its residual 6.6% stake in Yakult Honsha for approximately €500&nbsp;million, while retaining its joint ventures and partnership with the company.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone to sell remaining €500 million stake in Japan's Yakult | url = https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/danone-sell-remaining-500-million-euro-stake-japans-yakult-2020-10-06/ | website = Reuters | date = 6 October 2020 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Internal reorganization and governance crisis (2020–2021) ===

In November 2020 management announced, as part of its Local First plan, the elimination of 1,500 to 2,000 positions, including nearly 500 in France, to increase profitability and achieve €1&nbsp;billion in savings by 2023. This prompted sharp criticism as the group simultaneously announced that it was highly profitable and had just returned €1.4&nbsp;billion to shareholders.<ref>{{cite web | title = Emmanuel Faber : « Une entreprise comme Danone ne tourne pas sans actionnaires » | url = https://www.liberation.fr/france/2020/11/24/emmanuel-faber-une-entreprise-comme-danone-ne-tourne-pas-sans-actionnaires_1806569/ | website = Libération | date = 24 November 2020 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Danone annonce la suppression de 1 500 à 2 000 postes dans le monde| url = https://www.lsa-conso.fr/danone-annonce-la-suppression-de-1-500-a-2-000-postes-dans-le-monde,365903| website = LSA | date = 23 November 2020 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In late January 2021 the arrival of investment fund Bluebell Capital as a shareholder of Danone called into question the presence of [[Emmanuel Faber]] at the head of Danone.<ref>{{cite web | title = Le fonds activiste Bluebell réclamerait le départ du PDG de Danone Emmanuel Faber | url = https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/le-fonds-activiste-bluebell-reclamerait-le-depart-du-pdg-de-danone-emmanuel-faber.N1050244 | website = L’Usine Nouvelle | date = 27 January 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In a letter sent to all shareholders in November 2020, Bluebell Capital deplored the "disappointing" stock market performance and argued that under Emmanuel Faber's chairmanship, "the right balance between shareholder value creation and sustainability issues" had not been respected.<ref>{{cite web | title = Le PDG de Danone sous pression d'un fonds activiste | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2021/01/19/le-pdg-de-danone-sous-pression-d-un-fonds-activiste_6066779_3234.html | website = Le Monde| date = 19 January 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In February 2021 Danone announced the acquisition of Earth Island, an American company specializing in plant-based products.<ref>{{cite web | title = France's Danone buys U.S. plant-based foods firm Earth Island| url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-danone-m-a/frances-danone-buys-u-s-plant-based-foods-firm-earth-island-idUSKBN2AJ0H3/| website = Reuters | date = 18 February 2021| access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

On 1 March 2021 the decision to once again separate the roles of chairman and chief executive was taken by the group's board of directors following pressure from Bluebell Capital and Artisan Partners. Both funds called on 3 March 2021<ref>{{cite web | title = Comment le nouveau patron de Danone veut relancer le groupe| url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/comment-le-nouveau-patron-de-danone-veut-relancer-le-groupe-20220221 | website = Le Figaro | date = 21 February 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> for Faber's removal from the chairmanship.<ref>{{cite web

| title = Pour Artisan Partners, c'est une erreur d'avoir maintenu Emmanuel Faber à la présidence | url = https://www.latribune.fr/entreprises-finance/industrie/agroalimentaire-biens-de-consommation-luxe/danone-pour-artisan-partners-c-est-une-erreur-d-avoir-maintenu-emmanuel-faber-a-la-presidence-879032.html | website = La Tribune | date = 2 March 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In March 2021 [[Emmanuel Faber]] was dismissed from his position, with shareholders considering that the company was becoming less profitable due to its corporate social and environmental responsibility policy.<ref>{{cite web | title = L'affaire Danone pose la question du sens de la RSE | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/idees-debats/editos-analyses/laffaire-danone-pose-la-question-du-sens-de-la-rse-1300982| website = Les Échos | date = 17 March 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In early April 2021 Danone's reorganization plan was launched:<ref>{{cite web| title = Réorganisation chez Danone : le groupe prévoit 1 850 suppressions de postes dans le monde | url = https://www.bfmtv.com/economie/reorganisation-chez-danone-le-groupe-precise-prevoir-1850-suppressions-de-postes-dans-le-monde_AD-202104010231.html| website = BFMTV | date = 1 April 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> it provided for the elimination of 1,850 positions worldwide, including 458 in France.<ref>{{cite web| title = Danone : la suppression de plus de 500 postes en France confirmée| url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2021/04/01/danone-la-suppression-de-plus-de-500-postes-en-france-confirmee_6075287_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 1 April 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> A few weeks later, the general meeting approved the payment of a dividend of €1.94 per share for 2020 results, representing a total of €1.3&nbsp;billion returned to shareholders.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone – Assemblée Générale 2021 : approbation de toutes les résolutions| url = https://www.zonebourse.com/cours/action/DANONE-4634/actualite/DANONE-Assemblee-Generale-2021-approbation-de-toutes-les-resolutions-33111989/| website = ZoneBourse | date = 29 April 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> By end of June 2021, the full scope of the redundancy plan was revealed: 1,200 positions were eliminated, notably among senior management, managers, sales staff, and assistants. In parallel, 770 positions were to be created.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone : le plan social concernerait près de 1 200 postes en France | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2021/06/30/danone-le-plan-social-concernerait-pres-de-1-200-postes-en-france_6086360_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 30 June 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Renew strategy and refocusing of the brand portfolio around health (since 2021) ===

In September 2021 [[Antoine de Saint-Affrique]] was officially appointed chief executive officer of Danone.<ref>{{cite web | title = Un nouveau patron pour Danone après un an de crises | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/flash-eco/un-nouveau-patron-pour-danone-apres-un-an-de-crises-20210910 | website = Le Figaro | date = 10 September 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> This appointment came a few months after that of [[Gilles Schnepp]] as chairman of the board of directors.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone nomme Gilles Schnepp président avec effet immédiat, Faber quitte le groupe | url = https://investir.lesechos.fr/2021/03/danone-nomme-gilles-schnepp-president-avec-effet-immediat-faber-quitte-le-groupe-1842557 | website = Les Échos – Investir | date = 15 March 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> This governance change came in the context of performance deemed insufficient by a portion of shareholders and financial markets.<ref>{{cite web | title = L'année où Danone aura revu sa gouvernance de fond en comble | url = https://www.novethic.fr/finance-durable/tendances-de-marche/lannee-ou-danone-aura-revu-sa-gouvernance-de-fond-en-comble | website = Novethic | date = 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In March 2022 de Saint-Affrique presented his Renew Danone plan, which he intended to enable the company to return to profitable and sustainable growth.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone veut revenir à une culture de performance | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/conso-distribution/danone-veut-revenir-a-une-culture-de-performance-1391971 | website = Les Échos | date = 8 March 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> The plan rested notably on more active portfolio management, stronger financial discipline, and a refocusing on categories identified as priorities, particularly specialized nutrition, health, and certain high-value-added proteins.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone commence à faire tourner son portefeuille | url = https://www.wansquare.com/012-36001-Danone-commence-a-faire-tourner-son-portefeuille.html | website = Wansquare | date = 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> This strategic direction translated into several asset reallocation decisions during the year. In May in particular, Danone announced the end of its partnership with the Chinese group [[Mengniu]], while recovering control of the Dumex Baby Food infant nutrition brand.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone reorganises China assets in deal with Yashili | url = https://www.reuters.com/business/danone-reorganises-china-assets-deal-with-yashili-2022-05-06/ | website = Reuters | date = 6 May 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

During the same period the group temporarily increased its deliveries of infant formula to the United States to address a national shortage,<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone augmente ses exportations de lait infantile aux États-Unis, victimes de pénurie | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/danone-augmente-ses-exportations-de-lait-infantile-aux-etats-unis-victimes-de-penurie-20220527 | website = Le Figaro | date = 27 May 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> at the request of US authorities.

In February 2023 Danone inaugurated a new international research and innovation center on the [[Paris-Saclay]] plateau at a cost of €100&nbsp;million. The construction of the site was part of a property and industrial project aimed at consolidating research and development activities previously spread across multiple sites.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone : un nouveau centre de recherche en santé à Paris-Saclay | url = https://pharmaceutiques.com/actualites/entreprises/danone-un-nouveau-centre-de-recherche-en-sante-a-paris-saclay/ | website = Pharmaceutiques | date = 2023 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

Alongside its restructuring, the group faced major geopolitical developments. In October 2022, Danone announced its intention to disengage from Russia, where it employed more than 7,000 people, following [[Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022]] and the associated sanctions.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone choisit de solder son aventure en Russie | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2022/10/14/danone-choisit-de-solder-son-aventure-en-russie_6145762_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 14 October 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In July 2023, the Russian state took control of Danone's assets in the country,<ref>{{cite web | title = Russia seizes control of shares in Danone and Carlsberg subsidiaries | url = https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/17/russia-seizes-control-of-shares-in-danone-and-carlsberg-subsidiaries | website = The Guardian | date = 17 July 2023 | access-date = 29 June 2026}}</ref> leading the group to deconsolidate these activities, which represented approximately 5% of its global turnover.<ref>{{cite web | title = La Russie revenue à 5% du chiffre d'affaires de Danone, le marché rassuré | url = https://investir.lesechos.fr/2022/02/la-russie-revenue-a-5-du-chiffre-daffaires-de-danone-le-marche-rassure-1857103 | website = Les Échos – Investir | date = 2022 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In March 2024, these activities were ultimately sold to a close associate of [[Ramzan Kadyrov]] for the equivalent of €177&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone annonce avoir reçu les autorisations de Moscou pour céder sa filiale russe | url = https://www.lemonde.fr/economie/article/2024/03/22/danone-annonce-avoir-recu-les-autorisations-de-moscou-pour-ceder-sa-filiale-russe-a-un-proche-du-dirigeant-tchetchene-ramzan-kadyrov_6223633_3234.html | website = Le Monde | date = 22 March 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> Asset write-downs related to this disposal are estimated at more than €1&nbsp;billion.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone va céder une activité en Russie et déprécier jusqu'à 1 milliard | url = https://www.agefi.fr/news/entreprises/danone-va-ceder-une-activite-en-russie-et-deprecier-jusqua-1-milliard | website = L’Agefi | date = 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

Still a priority for the group, portfolio rotation accelerated in early 2024 with the announcement of the disposal of its organic dairy product activities in the United States, comprising the Horizon Organic and Wallaby brands, to the American investment firm Platinum Equity.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone vend ses activités de produits laitiers biologiques aux États-Unis à Platinum Equity | url = https://www.challenges.fr/economie/danone-vend-ses-activites-de-produits-laitiers-biologiques-aux-etats-unis-a-platinum-equity_878756 | website = Challenges | date = 2 January 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> These activities represented approximately 3% of the group's turnover.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone vend ses deux marques américaines de produits bio à un fonds d'investissement | url = https://www.bfmtv.com/economie/entreprises/danone-vend-ses-deux-marques-americaines-de-produits-bio-a-un-fonds-d-investissement_AD-202401020181.html | website = BFMTV | date = 2 January 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> The sales of these brands was presented in the financial press as a concrete application of the Renew strategic plan, aimed at concentrating investments on segments considered more promising in terms of growth and profitability, while focusing more squarely on health and medical nutrition. In February 2024, Danone announced an investment of €43&nbsp;million in the refitting of its factory in the Gers, at [[Villecomtal-sur-Arros]], now dedicated to the production of plant-based proteins.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone inaugure à Villecomtal sa nouvelle usine de production | url = https://gazette-du-midi.fr/au-sommaire/entreprises/danone-inaugure-a-villecomtal-32-sa-nouvelle-usine-de-production-de-jus-d | website = Gazette du Midi | date = 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In June the group declared its intention to focus further on health and medical nutrition to increase its sales.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone mise sur la santé pour doper sa croissance | url = https://investir.lesechos.fr/actu-des-valeurs/la-vie-des-actions/danone-mise-sur-la-sante-pour-doper-sa-croissance-2102668 | website = Les Échos – Investir | date = 2024 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> This direction translated into several targeted acquisitions. In May 2025, Danone announced the acquisition of a majority stake in the American company Kate Farms,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Danone double de taille dans la nutrition médicale aux États-Unis |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/danone-double-de-taille-dans-la-nutrition-medicale-aux-etats-unis-20250512 |archive-date= |website=lefigaro |date=12 May 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Danone va doubler de taille dans la nutrition médicale aux Etats-Unis |url=https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/conso-distribution/danone-va-doubler-de-taille-dans-la-nutrition-medicale-aux-etats-unis-2164621 |website=les echos}}</ref> specializing in medical nutrition, for an undisclosed amount.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone va doubler de taille dans la nutrition médicale aux États-Unis | url = https://www.lesechos.fr/industrie-services/conso-distribution/danone-va-doubler-de-taille-dans-la-nutrition-medicale-aux-etats-unis-2164621 | website = Les Échos | date = 12 May 2025 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Danone double de taille dans la nutrition médicale aux États-Unis | url = https://www.lefigaro.fr/societes/danone-double-de-taille-dans-la-nutrition-medicale-aux-etats-unis-20250512 | website = Le Figaro | date = 12 May 2025 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> On 25 June 2025, the group also acquired the Belgian company The Akkermansia Company, specializing in research on biotics and gut microbiota.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone acquiert le groupe belge The Akkermansia Company | url = https://www.lecho.be/entreprises/pharma-biotechnologie/danone-acquiert-le-groupe-belge-the-akkermansia-company-et-mise-sur-les-biotiques-de-nouvelle-generation/10613376.html | website = L’Echo | date = 25 June 2025 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

In March 2026 Danone announced the signing of an agreement to acquire the British company Huel, specializing in ready-to-consume meal solutions and nutritionally balanced products, marketed primarily through direct-to-consumer online sales. This acquisition is part of the group's continued recentering toward functional nutrition and health-related consumption segments.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone poursuit sa stratégie en misant sur la santé : le groupe va acquérir Huel | url = https://www.bfmtv.com/economie/entreprises/danone-poursuit-sa-strategie-en-misant-sur-la-sante-le-groupe-va-acquerir-huel-specialiste-britannique-des-repas-instantanes-proteines_AD-202603230491.html | website = BFMTV | date = 23 March 2026 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> In August 2026, the deal was cleared by the [[Competition and Markets Authority]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-20 |title=Danone €1bn takeover of Tring based Huel approved by watchdog |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crl7y671w8go |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Corporate governance ==

=== Company leadership ===
From 1966 to 2014, Danone was led by a single chairman and chief executive officer:

* [[Antoine Riboud]]: 1966–1996 
* [[Franck Riboud]]: 1996–2014

On 1 September 2014, Danone's governance evolved with the separation of the chairman and chief executive roles and the establishment of a strengthened chairmanship:

* chairman of the board of directors: [[Franck Riboud]] 
* chief executive officer and vice-chairman of the board: [[Emmanuel Faber]]

In 2017, Emmanuel Faber was appointed chairman and chief executive officer, succeeding Franck Riboud, who became honorary chairman.

In March 2021 the board of directors of Danone decided once again to separate the roles of chairman and chief executive, on the proposal of Emmanuel Faber who was to retain the chairmanship but hand over the chief executive function.<ref>{{cite web | title = Danone : Emmanuel Faber gardera la présidence, maintenu temporairement comme PDG | url = https://www.bfmtv.com/economie/danone-emmanuel-faber-gardera-la-presidence-maintenu-temporairement-comme-pdg_AD-202103010454.html | website = BFMTV | date = 1 March 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref> On 14 March, however, the board decided to remove Emmanuel Faber with immediate effect and to replace him on an interim basis by [[Gilles Schnepp]], former chairman and chief executive officer of Legrand.

In May 2021 a report in [[Le Figaro]] announced the appointment of [[Antoine Bernard de Saint-Affrique]] to succeed [[Emmanuel Faber]] as the group's chief executive officer from September 2021.<ref>{{cite web | title = Antoine de Saint-Affrique va succéder à Emmanuel Faber à la tête de Danone | url = https://www.bfmtv.com/economie/entreprises/antoine-de-saint-affrique-va-succeder-a-emmanuel-faber-a-la-tete-de-danone_AD-202105170017.html | website = BFMTV | date = 17 May 2021 | access-date = 25 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Board of directors ===
As of 14 December 2024 the 11 members of the board of directors are as follows:

* [[Gilles Schnepp]] – chairman of the board of directors 
* [[Valérie Chapoulaud-Floquet]] – Lead director, independent director 
* [[Frédéric Boutebba]] – Political and social affairs, non-independent director 
* [[Antoine de Saint-Affrique]] – chief executive officer, non-independent director 
* [[Gilbert Ghostine]] – Chairman of the Sandoz board of directors, independent director 
* [[Lise Kingo]] – Company director, chair of the CSR committee, independent director 
* [[Patrice Louvet]] – President and chief executive officer of Polo Ralph Lauren, member of the nomination, remuneration and governance committee, independent director 
* [[Sanjiv Mehta (Indian businessman)|Sanjiv Mehta]] – Company director, member of the audit committee, independent director 
* [[Géraldine Picaud]] – chief executive officer of SGS, chair of the audit committee, independent director 
* [[Susan Roberts]] – Associate Dean for fundamental research, Professor of Medicine and Epidemiology, member of the CSR committee, independent director 
* [[Bettina Theissig]] – Director representing employees and member of the CSR committee, non-independent director.

== Ownership ==
Ownership of Danone is split as follows: 43% is owned by American investors, 19% by French investors, followed by the UK (10%), Switzerland (6%), Germany (5%) and the rest of Europe (17%).<ref>{{cite web |date=7 November 2019 |title=Danone's ownership – Danone |url=https://www.danone.com/investor-relations/danone-at-a-glance/ownership.html}}</ref>

== Joint ventures ==
In some areas, Danone has adopted a strategy of growth through joint ventures, particularly in fast-growing emerging markets which represent over 50% of its sales.<ref name=WSJ>James T. Areddy  & Deborah Ball, [https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB118184992493235680?mod=googlenews_wsj Danone's China Strategy Is Set Back] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200622205641/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB118184992493235680?mod=googlenews_wsj |date=22 June 2020 }}, ''The Wall Street Journal'', Page A10, 15 June 2007</ref>

Danone signed joint ventures with Al Safi in Saudi Arabia (2001),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.alsafi-danone.com.sa/History.html |title=تم تعليق النطاق &#124; Domain suspended |access-date=12 March 2008 |archive-date=1 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701034716/http://www.alsafi-danone.com.sa/History.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Yakult]] in India (2005) and Vietnam (2006), Alquería in Colombia (2007), and [[Mengniu]] in China (2013–2014).<ref name=WSJ/>

=== Australia ===
Danone Murray Goulburn is a joint [[Saputo Inc.|Saputo Dairy Australia]] venture with French food company Danone – to market yoghurt and other fresh dairy products in Australia. Danone-MG dairy foods are produced at Kiewa in north east Victoria and are sold throughout Australia.

=== Bangladesh ===
In November 2005 Franck Riboud met [[Muhammad Yunus]], founder of the [[Grameen Bank]] and later winner of the [[2006 Nobel Peace Prize]]. The two men discussed at length their ideas on the development of poor countries and found that their areas of expertise were complementary.<ref>{{cite news |date=5 March 2012 |title=RICHARD BRANSON: Profit is not all that matters|url=http://www.bdlive.co.za/articles/2012/03/05/richard-branson-profit-is-not-all-that-matters|newspaper=Business Day|location=South Africa}}</ref> As a result, in 2006, the Grameen Bank and Danone formed a company called [[Grameen Danone]] Foods, a [[social business]] in Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ahmad |first=Reaz |date=13 March 2006 |title=Grameen teams up with Groupe Danone to set up food plant |url=http://thedailystar.net/2006/03/13/d60313011410.htm |newspaper=The Daily Star}}</ref>

Grameen Danone Foods Ltd produces a yoghurt called Shokti Doi containing [[protein]], [[vitamins]], iron, [[calcium]], [[zinc]], and other [[micronutrients]] aimed to fill nutritional deficits of children in Bangladesh. Shokti Doi is sold for six euro cents, a price that studies found to be affordable for the poorest families. Its pursuit of profitability is based solely on criteria such as improving public health, creating jobs, reducing poverty and protecting the environment.{{Promotion inline|date=February 2022}} Profits earned by the company are re-invested in expanding and running the business.

=== India ===
Danone started its nutrition business in India in 2012 through the acquisition of the nutrition portfolio from [[Wockhardt Group]].<ref>{{cite news |date=26 July 2012 |title=Danone completes acquisition of Wockhardt Group's nutrition business|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/danone-completes-acquisition-of-wockhardt-groups-nutrition-business/articleshow/15164816.cms|newspaper=The Economic Times}}</ref> Danone India offers a range of specialized products across life stages that includes pregnancy, infants, young children as well as adults, under Indian and global brands like Aptamil, Neocate, Farex, Protinex, Dexolac and Nusobee. Headquartered in Mumbai.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.danone.in/ |title=Home |website=danone.in}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=January 2021}} In 2018, Danone reduced its product portfolio and discontinued some dairy SKUs to bring a sharper focus on its nutrition offerings.<ref>{{cite news |date=11 January 2018 |title=Danone India to rationalise its product portfolio|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/danone-india-to-rationalise-its-product-portfolio/article10027069.ece|newspaper=Business Line}}</ref>

=== Israel ===
In March 1996 Danone signed an agreement to purchase 20 percent of the [[Strauss Group]], Israel's second largest food manufacturer. Since the 1970s, Strauss Dairies had a series of partnership and knowledge agreements with Danone.

=== Saudi Arabia ===
In 2001 [[Al Faisaliah Group|Al-Safi]] and Danone formed a partnership.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 August 2017 |title=World first for Al Safi Danone |url=https://www.tetrapak.com/en-us/insights/cases-articles/al-safi-danone |access-date=27 January 2025 |website=Tetra Pak}}</ref>

=== China ===
Danone has invested in China since 1987 with the joint venture with [[Fengxing Milk]] in Guangzhou. It is one of Danone's top 5 markets.{{citation needed|date=July 2017}}

==== Bright Dairy ====
In 2001 Danone acquired a 5% stake in Bright Dairy and, in March 2005, doubled its shareholding,<ref>[http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/200503/04/eng20050304_175531.html Danone to double Bright Dairy stake] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071227141245/http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/200503/04/eng20050304_175531.html |date=27 December 2007 }}, ''People's Daily'', 4 March 2005</ref> and again, to 20%, in April 2006, becoming the third largest shareholder after Shanghai Milk Group and S.I. Food.

The parties announced in October 2007 that Danone would divest its stake by selling it to the other two main shareholders at a small profit.<ref name=xinhua/> Bright Dairy said Danone would pay 330m yuan (€31m) to terminate the existing distribution and production agreement with it.<ref>Neil Merrett, [http://www.dairyreporter.com/news/ng.asp?n=80638-danone-dairy-bright-wahaha Danone sells Chinese dairy stake] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071227165244/http://www.dairyreporter.com/news/ng.asp?n=80638-danone-dairy-bright-wahaha |date=27 December 2007 }}, ''Dairy Reporter'', 17 October 2007</ref>

==== Wahaha ====
{{Main|Wahaha Joint Venture Company}}
The [[Hangzhou Wahaha Group]], the largest beverage producer in China,<ref name="scmp">{{Cite news |work=South China Morning Post |location=Hong Kong |title = Danone set to sue Wahaha over breach of contract |date = 11 April 2007 |page = B3}}</ref> and Danone entered into a dairy products joint venture in 1996, in which Danone held 51%. It was hailed by ''[[Forbes]]'' magazine as a "showcase" joint venture.<ref name="forbes070627">{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/feeds/ap/2007/06/27/ap3861182.html |author=Elaine Kurtenbach |title=Wahaha-Danone Feud Highlights Pitfalls |work=Forbes |date=27 June 2007 |access-date=17 July 2007 }}{{dead link|date=January 2022|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Yet in 2005 Danone noted that alongside the 39 structures of the joint venture, 60 factories and distribution companies produce and sell beverages illegally under the Wahaha brand. Danone made several attempts to take a stake in the Wahaha companies external to the joint venture, but was rebuffed by Wahaha's general manager Zong Qinghou.<ref name="scmp2">{{Cite news |work=South China Morning Post |location=Hong Kong |title = Danone and Wahaha vie for the last laugh |date = 11 June 2007 |page = B3}}</ref> Danone and Zong Qinghou had signed a deal in December 2006 allowing Danone to buy a majority stake in these non-JV operations. However, Zong had second thoughts about the deal and reneged, claiming the offer was underpriced and held out for a higher price from Danone.<ref name=caijin4>签约与悔约(regrets) [http://www.caijing.com.cn/industry/other/2007-05-13/19400.shtml ''Wahaha – atypical commercial dispute''] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080308211340/http://www.caijing.com.cn/industry/other/2007-05-13/19400.shtml |date=8 March 2008 }}, ''[[Caijing]]'' Issue 185, 14 May 2007 {{in lang|zh}}</ref>

The dispute took on the shape of a trademark dispute, and Danone filed for arbitration in [[Stockholm]] on 9 May 2007.<ref name=xinhua>[[Xinhua]], [http://english.eastday.com/eastday/englishedition/business/userobject1ai2914641.html Wahaha says its arbitration application accepted over trademark dispute with Danone] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071227214916/http://english.eastday.com/eastday/englishedition/business/userobject1ai2914641.html |date=27 December 2007 }}, 18 June 2007</ref> On 4 June,<ref name="release2">{{Cite press release|url=http://www.danone.com/wps/portal/jump/DanoneCorporateIntl.Press.Commun2004PressReleases?ref=CMS.DanoneCorporateIntl.Press.2006PressReleases.Trimestre1.CP_120607 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927210545/http://www.danone.com/wps/portal/jump/DanoneCorporateIntl.Press.Commun2004PressReleases?ref=CMS.DanoneCorporateIntl.Press.2006PressReleases.Trimestre1.CP_120607 |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 September 2007 |publisher=Danone Group |title=current developments regarding Wahaha dispute |date=12 June 2007 |access-date=21 June 2007 }}</ref> Danone filed suit in Los Angeles Superior Court against Ever Maple Trading and Hangzhou Hongsheng Beverage Co Ltd, companies controlled by Zong, his wife, and daughter.<ref name=france24>[http://www.france24.com/france24Public/en/news/business/20070618-danone-wahaha-china-france-food-companies.html Danone, Wahaha set for arbitration dispute in China] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070621215709/http://www.france24.com/france24Public/en/news/business/20070618-danone-wahaha-china-france-food-companies.html |date=21 June 2007 }}, [[Agence France-Presse]] story, France 24, 18 June 2007</ref>

In 2009 an agreement was reached between the two parties. Danone left the Danone–Wahaha joint venture and sold its shares (51%) to its former Chinese partner.

==== Mengniu ====
On 20 May 2013 Danone announced a strategic investment (4.0%) in Mengniu, the top dairy products company in China, through an agreement with COFCO (the state-owned largest food company in China a majority shareholder in Mengniu). Later on, Danone raised its interest in Mengniu from 4.0% to 9.9%. In 2016, Danone is Mengniu's second shareholder.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 May 2013 |title=Danone hopes to crack China with new dairy deal|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/chinamengniu-danone-idUSL3N0E104420130520 |work=Reuters}}</ref>

In addition, in May 2013 a joint-venture was created between Danone and Mengniu to grow the fresh dairy product category.<ref>{{cite news |date=11 February 2014 |title=Danone to double stake in China Mengniu to 9.9 pct for $665 mln|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/mengniu-danone-idUSL3N0LH0WU20140212|work=Reuters}}</ref>

On 31 October 2014 Danone, Mengniu and Yashili announced that they had signed an agreement allowing Danone to take part in a private placement by Yashili totalling €437&nbsp;million, at a price of HK$3.70 per share. Upon completion of the subscription, Mengniu and Danone respectively held 51.0% and 25.0% equity interest in Yashili.<ref>{{cite news |date=24 July 2015 |title=Danone swaps Dumex China unit for deeper ties with domestic dairy giant|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/yashili-danone-idUSL3N1041DQ20150724|work=Reuters}}</ref>

=== Russia ===
On 18 June 2010 Danone partnered with Unimilk, one of Russia's main milk producers. Danone and Unimilk merged their fresh dairy products activities in Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Belarus. The joint-venture gave birth to the number one dairy products company in this region. Russia became one of the five most important markets for Danone.<ref>{{cite news |date=18 June 2010 |title=Danone secures Russia expansion with Unimilk deal|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-danone-unimilk-idUSTRE65H27A20100618|work=Reuters}}</ref>

In October 2022 Danone announced the start of the process of transferring its Russian segment to new owners. By this point, Russia provided about 5% of the company's total revenue.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.danone.com/content/dam/danone-corp/danone-com/investors/en-all-publications/2022/pressreleases/danone141022pr.pdf|title=Danone announces it plans to transfer the effective control of its EDP business in Russia|date=14 October 2022|website=danone.com|access-date=14 October 2022|archive-date=14 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014091002/https://www.danone.com/content/dam/danone-corp/danone-com/investors/en-all-publications/2022/pressreleases/danone141022pr.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> The company considered about two dozen possible applicants for its assets, but as of July 2023, the "successor" has not been decided. In the meantime, Danone rebranded one of its top brands: Activia in the Russian market becoming Aktibio. The company said that this will allow renewed investment in the Russian dairy industry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ria.ru/20230710/aktivia-1883294176.html|title=Торговая марка "Активиа" сменит название в России|language=ru|date=10 July 2023|website=[[RIA Novosti]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.danone.ru/fileadmin/user_upload/DanoneRussia/NEWs/2023/press-reliz-aktibio-10-07-2023.pdf|title=Актибио (press release)|language=ru|date=10 July 2023|website=Danone.ru|access-date=10 July 2023|archive-date=10 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230710125808/https://www.danone.ru/fileadmin/user_upload/DanoneRussia/NEWs/2023/press-reliz-aktibio-10-07-2023.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July 2023, the Russian government seized the shares in Danone Russia and placed it under the control of the Russian [[Federal Agency for State Property Management]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Russia seizes control of Danone and Carlsberg operations |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-66218999 |date=17 July 2023}}</ref> On 18 July, Ibragim Zakriev, the Minister of Agriculture of [[Chechnya]] and the nephew of its President [[Ramzan Kadyrov]], was appointed General Director of the Russian Danone.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rbc.ru/business/18/07/2023/64b6d69b9a79470efe619633|title=Гендиректором «дочки» Danone в России стал глава минсельхоза Чечни|language=ru|date=18 July 2023|website=Rbc.ru}}</ref> As of 26 July 2023 Danone has provided €700&nbsp;million for the loss of Russian business, plus €500&nbsp;million exchange loss due to the fall in the ruble.<ref>{{cite web |title=Danone Writes Down Russia Assets, Beats On Like-For-Like Sales |url=https://www.checkout.ie/a-brands/danone-writes-down-russia-assets-beats-on-like-for-like-sales-203920 |date=26 July 2023}}</ref>

Centrale Laitière is Danone's first franchise ever: the companies have worked together since 1953.<ref>{{cite news |date=27 June 2012 |title=Danone to take control of Centrale Laitiere |newspaper=Financial Times |url=http://www.ft.com/intl/cms/s/eaf73470-c084-11e1-982d-00144feabdc0, |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20221210/http://www.ft.com/intl/cms/s/eaf73470-c084-11e1-982d-00144feabdc0, |archive-date=10 December 2022}}</ref>

In October 2013 Danone teamed up with Abraaj Group to acquire FanMilk International, the leading manufacturer and distributor of frozen dairy products and juices in [[Ghana]], [[Togo]], [[Nigeria]], [[Burkina Faso]], [[Benin]] and [[Ivory Coast]].<ref>{{cite news |date=24 October 2013 |title=Danone to join Abraaj Group in Fan Milk International acquisition |url=http://www.cnbcafrica.com/news/western-africa/2013/10/24/danone-to-join-abraaj-group-in-fan-milk-international-acquisition/ |publisher=CNBC |access-date=17 June 2016 |archive-date=17 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817225648/http://www.cnbcafrica.com/news/western-africa/2013/10/24/danone-to-join-abraaj-group-in-fan-milk-international-acquisition/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
