== Timeline ==

=== April ===
The ship departed from [[Ushuaia]] on 1 April with 175 passengers and crew.<ref name="oceanwide 8may">{{Cite web |title=Press update {{!}} m/v Hondius: 8 May 2026, 19:00 hrs CET |url=https://oceanwide-expeditions.com/press/press-update-m-v-hondius-8-may-2026-19-00-hrs-cet |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=Oceanwide Expeditions  |language=en}}</ref> On 6 April, a 70-year-old Dutch man began showing symptoms,<ref name="carroll-2026"/> and he died on board on 11 April,<ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /><ref name="carroll-2026" /> initially attributed to generic [[natural causes]].<ref name="carroll-2026" /> The ship stopped at the [[British Overseas Territory]] of [[Tristan da Cunha]] on 13–15 April.<ref name="green">{{Cite news |last=Green |first=Kelly |title=Visit of the Cruise Ship MV Hondius, April 2026 |url=https://www.tristandc.com/shipping/news-2026-04-17-hondius.php |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=Tristan da Cunha Visit News }}</ref><ref name="kendall-2026a">{{Cite news |last=Kendall |first=Philip |title=Suspected Hantavirus on the Cruise Ship MV Hondius |url=https://www.tristandc.com/government/news-2026-05-04-hondius-hantavirus.php |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=Tristan da Cunha Government News |ref={{harvid|Kendall|2026a}} }}</ref> On 24 April, the Dutchman's body was taken off the ship<ref name="aikman-2026" /><ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /> upon the ship's arrival at the British Overseas Territory of [[Saint Helena]]. At this time, 29 passengers disembarked the ship; among them was the man's 69-year-old widow, who later took a plane to South Africa.<ref>{{cite news |date=7 May 2026 |title=Dozens of passengers left hantavirus-stricken cruise ship after 1st fatality |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/health/dozens-of-passengers-left-hantavirus-stricken-cruise-ship-after-1st-fatality |publisher=PBS |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Oceanwide-2026a">{{Cite press release |title=M/V Hondius: 7 May 2026, 11:30 hrs CET |url=https://oceanwide-expeditions.com/press/press-update-m-v-hondius-7-may-2026-11-30-hrs-cet |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[Oceanwide Expeditions]] |language=en }}</ref> The disembarked passengers were from 12 countries and returned home before [[contact tracing]] began.<ref name="ctv 7may" />

On 25 April, the widow, who had unknowingly contracted the virus, boarded [[KLM]] flight KL592 from [[Johannesburg]] to [[Amsterdam]], but she was removed from the plane before takeoff due to her medical condition,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Passenger with hantavirus was briefly on board a KLM aircraft in Johannesburg |url=https://news.klm.com/passenger-with-hantavirus-was-briefly-on-board-a-klm-aircraft-in-johannesburg/ |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=KLM Newsroom |language=en |archive-date=8 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508090211/https://news.klm.com/passenger-with-hantavirus-was-briefly-on-board-a-klm-aircraft-in-johannesburg/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and she died in a hospital in South Africa on 26 April.<ref name="aikman-2026" /> The widow was on the plane for 45 minutes.<ref name="rtl 7may">{{Cite web |date=7 May 2026 |title=GGD: vijf inzittenden KLM-vlucht hadden intensief contact met hanta-slachtoffer |trans-title=GGD: Five passengers on a KLM flight had close contact with a hantavirus victim |url=https://www.rtl.nl/nieuws/binnenland/artikel/5598861/zestig-mensen-beeld-voor-bron-en-contactonderzoek-hantavirus |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=RTL.nl |language=nl}}</ref> After stopping in Saint Helena, the ship continued on to the British Overseas Territory of [[Ascension Island]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Suspected Hantavirus on MV Hondius update |url=https://www.ascension.gov.ac/suspected-hantavirus-on-mv-hondius-update |website=Ascension Island Government |access-date=6 May 2026 |date=4 May 2026 }}</ref> where an ill British passenger was removed and flown to South Africa for hospital care. On 27 April, ''Hondius'' left Ascension Island.<ref>{{cite news |title=Health emergency on the MV Hondius: what we know |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260504-health-emergency-on-the-mv-hondius-what-we-know |access-date=6 May 2026 |work=[[France 24]] |date=4 May 2026 |language=en }}</ref>

=== May ===

==== 1–5 May ====
On 2 May, a German woman died on board,<ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /><ref name="Edwards-2026"/> and, {{as of|2026|5|8|alt=as of 8 May}}, her body remains on board the ship.<ref name="sample-2026">{{Cite news |last=Sample |first=Ian |date=7 May 2026 |title=Where did the cruise ship hantavirus come from and what happens next? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/07/where-cruise-ship-hantavirus-from-what-next-canary-islands |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 }}</ref> Following the identification of the outbreak on 4 May,<ref name="Oceanwide-2026a" /> passengers were told to limit close contact and frequently use [[hand sanitizer]].<ref name="parakozov-2026b">{{cite news |last1=Parakozov |first1=Sfundo |last2=Peyton |first2=Nellie |title=Two cases of hantavirus which spreads human-to-human linked to ship, South Africa says |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/two-cases-hantavirus-which-spreads-human-to-human-linked-ship-south-africa-says-2026-05-06/ |work=Reuters |date=6 May 2026 |access-date=7 May 2026 |ref={{harvid|Parakozov|2026b}} }}</ref> On 2 May, the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) first received a report of the hantavirus outbreak.<ref name="CNN/tenerife-arrive"/>

On 3 May, the ship docked in [[Praia]], the capital of [[Cape Verde]].<ref name="aikman-2026" /><ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /> The authorities said they were sending medical supplies and officials to support the ship, and officials in Praia also expanded safety protocols near the port as a precautionary measure.<ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /> The Cape Verdean government announced the creation of an isolation area and the coordination of a multidisciplinary team to assist the ship's passengers and crew.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lu |first=Donna |date=4 May 2026 |title=What is hantavirus, the infection thought to have killed three on cruise ship? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/may/04/what-is-hantavirus-the-infection-that-has-killed-three-people-on-a-cruise-ship |access-date=5 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://sicnoticias.pt/mundo/2026-05-04-oms-identifica-sete-casos-de-hantavirus-apos-surto-em-cruzeiro-de-luxo-6892ba49 |title=OMS identifica sete casos de hantavírus após surto em cruzeiro de luxo |website=[[SIC Notícias]] |access-date=5 May 2026 |language=pt |trans-title=WHO identifies seven cases of hantavirus after outbreak on luxury cruise ship }}</ref> Around the same time, South African officials began precautionary contact tracing.<ref name="asadu-risemberg-2026" /> By 4 May, gene sequencing had identified the Andes virus in at least one infected person.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goodman |first=Brenda |date=6 May 2026 |title=What doctors know about how the Andes hantavirus spreads |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/06/health/andes-strain-hantavirus-explained |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en }}</ref>

==== 6 May ====
[[File:LX-RHC (53416634236).jpg|thumb|right|The first evacuation flight was carried out by an air ambulance (LX-RHC) of [[Luxembourg Air Rescue]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 May 2026 |title=Luxembourg Air Rescue begins repatriation of two hantavirus cases from Dutch cruise ship |url=https://today.rtl.lu/news/luxembourg/luxembourg-air-rescue-reports-confusing-situation-in-cruise-ship-evacuation-346545019 |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=[[RTL Lëtzebuerg]] |language=en }}</ref>]]
On 6 May, the ship was anchored outside [[Cape Verde]], a country not deemed capable of dealing with the medical emergency on board.<ref name="aikman-2026" /> Despite the objections of the [[President of the Canary Islands|Canary Islands' regional president]], Spain approved the plan for the ''Hondius'' to dock in [[Tenerife]], citing its moral and legal obligation to the passengers.<ref name="the-independent-2026">{{Cite news |date=6 May 2026 |title='Why us?' Tenerife locals fear hantavirus cruise ship arrival to repeat Covid ordeal |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/tenerife-hantavirus-cruise-ship-covid-pandemic-b2971597.html |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=[[The Independent]] |language=en }}</ref>

The Swiss government confirmed that a man infected with hantavirus was being treated in [[Zurich]], Switzerland. Swiss authorities confirmed that the patient was a passenger on the cruise ship, bringing the total number of infections to eight.<ref name="SWI-6 May">{{Cite web |author=SWI |authorlink=SWI swissinfo |date=6 May 2026 |title=Man with hantavirus is being treated at Zurich University Hospital |url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/various/man-with-hantavirus-is-being-treated-at-zurich-university-hospital-switzerland/91371503 |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=swissinfo.ch |language=en }}</ref> The man was one of the 30 passengers who disembarked on 24 April.<ref name="McArthur-2026" /> On the same day, it was announced that three more people experiencing symptoms had been sent to the Netherlands by two [[air ambulance]]s for treatment; these were a 56-year-old Briton, a 41-year-old Dutch national, and a 65-year-old German, one of which was the ship's doctor.<ref name="aikman-2026" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2026 |title=Passagiers van schip met hantavirus geëvacueerd: Nederlander, Brit en Duitse |trans-title=Passengers on ship with hantavirus evacuated: a Dutch national, a British national, and a German national |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613323-passagiers-van-schip-met-hantavirus-geevacueerd-nederlander-brit-en-duitse |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=nos.nl |language=nl }}</ref><ref name="sample-2026" />

The first plane carrying two patients landed in the Netherlands on 6 May; the German national was later transferred to [[University Hospital of Düsseldorf]] and the Briton to [[Leiden University Medical Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2026 |title=Patiënt aangekomen bij LUMC • Tweede vliegtuig kampt met technische problemen |trans-title=Patient has arrived at LUMC • Second plane is experiencing technical difficulties |url=https://nos.nl/liveblog/2613369-patient-aangekomen-bij-lumc-tweede-vliegtuig-kampt-met-technische-problemen |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=nos.nl |language=nl }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Cruise ship hantavirus latest: British tour guide speaks to Sky News from hospital after evacuation |url=https://news.sky.com/story/three-dead-as-virus-breaks-out-on-atlantic-cruise-ship-13503266 |work=Sky News |date=6 May 2026 |access-date=7 May 2026 }}</ref> The second plane carrying the Dutch national diverted to [[Gran Canaria]] and awaited a replacement aircraft after experiencing technical issues in its life support systems.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cruise ship hantavirus latest: Patient in hospital in Switzerland – as Canary Islands refuses to let ship dock |url=https://news.sky.com/story/three-dead-as-virus-breaks-out-on-atlantic-cruise-ship-13503266?postid=11645016#liveblog-body |work=Sky News |date=7 May 2026 |access-date=7 May 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=6 May 2026 |title=El avión que lleva a dos pacientes con hantavirus para en Gran Canaria por un "fallo en el sistema eléctrico de soporte de un paciente" |trans-title=The plane carrying two patients with hantavirus made a stopover in Gran Canaria due to a 'malfunction in the patient life support system' |url=https://cadenaser.com/nacional/2026/05/06/el-avion-con-dos-evacuados-del-crucero-con-hantavirus-para-en-gran-canaria-por-una-averia-en-una-burbuja-de-aislamiento-cadena-ser/ |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=Cadena SER |language=es-ES }}</ref> On 6 May, the ship left Cape Verde for [[Spain]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Schadwinkel |first=Alina |date=6 May 2026 |title=(S+) Hantavirus auf Kreuzfahrtschiff MV »Hondius«: Fachleute sehen kein Pandemieszenario |url=https://www.spiegel.de/wissenschaft/medizin/hantavirus-auf-kreuzfahrtschiff-mv-hondius-fachleute-sehen-kein-pandemie-szenario-a-ed81ba53-de9c-454f-8109-ff1d0d3fce8d |access-date=6 May 2026 |work=Der Spiegel |language=de |issn=2195-1349 }}</ref> Four medical experts embarked while the ship was leaving Cape Verde. Two of these were medical specialists from [[Amsterdam University Medical Center]] and Central Military Hospital, a military hospital in [[Utrecht]]. The two others were epidemiologists from Italy and the Netherlands, meant to investigate the scope of the virus on the ship.<ref name="oceanwide 8may" /> The selection, transport, and coordination of these experts was assisted by the WHO and [[European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control]].<ref name="overheid.nl">{{Cite report|title=Medische evacuatie van cruiseschip m/v Hondius|publisher=Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken|date=6 May 2026|location=Den Haag|url=https://open.overheid.nl/details/c36611f5-3fde-4fea-a7d6-345aa3b73427|language=nl}}</ref>

Two anonymous Argentine investigators claimed that the leading hypothesis was that the [[index case]]—the Dutch citizen who showed the first symptoms—had contracted the virus.<ref name="Debre-AP">{{Cite web |last=Debre |first=Isabel |date=6 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus is on the rise in Argentina, where a stricken cruise ship began its journey |url=https://apnews.com/article/argentina-hantavirus-cruise-ship-5841c25be9aa6dd3cd6edc81c74609de |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[AP News]] |language=en }}</ref><ref name="grierson-2026a">{{Cite news |last=Grierson |first=Jamie |date=6 May 2026 |title=Three evacuated from hantavirus-hit ship as Spain says vessel can dock |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/06/cruise-ship-hantavirus-strain-andes-spread-humans-south-africa |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 }}</ref> On 6 May, the [[Ministry of Health (Argentina)|Argentine health ministry]] published a report detailing the movements of the index case, the Dutch citizen who presented the first symptoms, prior to the ship's departure; the report showed he had gone on a four-month road trip between 27 November 2025 and 1 April 2026, spanning Chile, Uruguay, and Argentina. Meanwhile, the National Ministry of Health and the [[Malbrán Institute]] are advancing the epidemiological investigation at the local level, capturing and testing rodents along the route the Dutch passenger travelled, as well as conducting [[contact tracing]]. The index case had returned to Argentina from Uruguay only four days before departure.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2026 |title=Argentina asiste a países europeos con insumos de diagnóstico para hantavirus |trans-title=Argentina is providing European countries with hantavirus testing supplies. |url=https://www.argentina.gob.ar/noticias/argentina-asiste-paises-europeos-con-insumos-de-diagnostico-para-hantavirus |access-date=6 May 2026 |website=[[Government of Argentina]] |language=es }}</ref>

==== 7 May ====
On 7 May, one of the flight attendants on the flight from [[Johannesburg]] to [[Amsterdam]] on 26 April was admitted to [[Amsterdam University Medical Center]] on suspicion of infection, having been in contact with the deceased Dutch woman.<ref name="nederlandse-omroep-stichting-2026">{{Cite news |date=7 May 2026 |title=Stewardess mogelijk ook besmet met hanta, ligt in Amsterdam UMC |trans-title=Flight attendant may also be infected with hantavirus; she is being treated at Amsterdam University Medical Center |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613426-stewardess-mogelijk-ook-besmet-met-hanta-ligt-in-amsterdam-umc |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]] |language=nl }}</ref> On 7 May, the diverted flight carrying the third patient from the ship landed in the Netherlands, and that patient was hospitalized at [[Radboud University Medical Center]].<ref name="nederlandse-omroep-stichting-2026" /> Later that day, the patient tested positive for the virus.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Groot |first1=Joep de Groot Verslaggever Profiel Joep de |last2=Groot |first2=Joep de Groot Verslaggever Profiel Joep de |date=7 May 2026 |title=Opgenomen patiënt in Radboudumc heeft hantavirus, WHO-topman noemt risico op besmetting laag |trans-title=A patient admitted to Radboud University Medical Center has hantavirus; WHO chief says risk of transmission is low|url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2026/05/07/opgenomen-patient-radboudumc-heeft-hantavirus-who-topman-noemt-risico-op-besmetting-laag-a4927285 |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=NRC |language=nl-NL }}</ref> The same day, the Singapore Communicable Diseases Agency announced that two of its residents who had been on the cruise and on the same flight as the Dutch woman from [[Saint Helena]] to Johannesburg—one of them symptomatic—were being tested.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship: Singapore residents tested |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/2-singapore-residents-on-hantavirus-hit-cruise-ship-isolated-at-ncid-and-undergoing-tests |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[The Straits Times]] |language=en |issn=0585-3923 |last=Mah |first=Alessia }}</ref> They tested negative on 8 May.<ref name="CNA">{{Cite web |title=Two Singapore residents who were on board hantavirus-hit cruise ship test negative: CDA |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/hantavirus-cruise-ship-mv-hondius-test-negative-quarantine-6109571 |access-date=12 May 2026 |website=CNA |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509075209/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/hantavirus-cruise-ship-mv-hondius-test-negative-quarantine-6109571|archive-date=2026-05-09|last=Kuek|first=Renee|url-status=live|date=2026-05-08}}</ref>

A comprehensive risk analysis of the individuals on the two flights the deceased woman had taken was completed by [[Municipal Health Service|GGD]] Kennemerland, the Dutch municipal health service responsible for [[Amsterdam Airport Schiphol]]. Five individuals were categorized as high risk for having assisted the woman in leaving [[KLM]] flight KL592; the hospitalized flight attendant is one of them. An additional 50 individuals were deemed lower risk, as they had been seated within two rows of the woman. The GGD is still attempting to contact these individuals.<ref name="rtl 7may" /> The remaining individuals have been informed and are considered to be at the lowest risk.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 May 2026 |title=Ziekenhuizen Nijmegen en Leiden stellen hantavirus vast bij opvarenden cruiseschip |trans-title=Nijmegen and Leiden hospitals have diagnosed hantavirus in cruise ship passengers |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613466-ziekenhuizen-nijmegen-en-leiden-stellen-hantavirus-vast-bij-opvarenden-cruiseschip |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting]] |language=nl }}</ref> From the first flight from Saint Helena to Johannesburg, three individuals have been tested due to symptoms; two of those tests have since come back negative.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 May 2026 |title=Twee vliegtuigpassagiers met klachten negatief getest op hantavirus |trans-title=Two airline passengers with symptoms have tested negative for hantavirus |url=https://www.ad.nl/binnenland/live-hantavirus-twee-vliegtuigpassagiers-met-klachten-negatief-getest-op-hantavirus~a3f98549 |website=[[Algemeen Dagblad]] |language=nl }}</ref>

It was reported that two patients had been identified as having the Andes virus in lab work by the [[National Institute for Communicable Diseases]] of South Africa.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Armstrong |first=Kathryn |date=7 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus-hit cruise ship on way to Canary Islands after three evacuated |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5y093d5n9ko |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[BBC News]] }}</ref> The same day, the [[UK Health Security Agency]] (UKHSA) told the [[BBC]] that all thirty people who left the ship during its stop in Saint Helena had been identified and contact traced.<ref name="roberts-2026" /> Two of these were Britons who are currently isolating without symptoms.<ref name="sample-2026" /> The Quebec Health Minister confirmed that three Canadians are isolating in [[Quebec]] and [[Ontario]]. Two of them disembarked in Saint Helena on 24 April, and the third flew on the same flight as the deceased woman to Johannesburg.<ref name="ctv 7may">{{Cite web |date=7 May 2026 |title=3 Canadians isolating following hantavirus outbreak on cruise. Live updates here. |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/article/3-canadians-isolating-following-hantavirus-outbreak-on-cruise-live-updates-here/ |access-date=7 May 2026 |website=CTVNews |language=en}}</ref> On 7 May, [[Oceanwide Expeditions]] said the ship was expected to arrive at the [[Port of Granadilla]], Tenerife, in the early hours of 10 May.<ref name="OE/update-7-may-2026-17-15">{{cite web |title=Press update {{!}} m/v Hondius: 7 May 2026, 17:15 hrs CET |url=https://oceanwide-expeditions.com/press/press-update-m-v-hondius-7-may-2026-17-15-hrs-cet |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507214205/https://oceanwide-expeditions.com/press/press-update-m-v-hondius-7-may-2026-17-15-hrs-cet |archive-date=7 May 2026 |website=[[Oceanwide Expeditions]] |access-date=9 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="cnn/2026/05/08/ship-hanta">{{cite news |last1=Cancryn |first1=Adam |last2=Goodman |first2=Brenda |last3=Hansler |first3=Jennifer |last4=McPhillips |first4=Deidre |last5=Stockwell |first5=Billy |title=CDC team to meet Americans on hantavirus-stricken ship as bad weather threatens landing |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/08/health/cruise-ship-hantavirus-passengers |access-date=9 May 2026 |work=[[CNN]] |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="scmp/3352939">{{cite news |title=Spain to repatriate guests as hantavirus-hit cruise ship heads for Canaries |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3352939/spain-repatriate-guests-hantavirus-hit-cruise-ship-heads-canaries |access-date=9 May 2026 |work=[[South China Morning Post]] |date=8 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==== 8 May ====
On 8 May, it was confirmed that the second British national in a health facility in South Africa, who had been on the same flight as the deceased Dutch woman, tested positive. Another Briton was suspected by the UKHSA of having contracted the virus on the island of [[Tristan da Cunha]], where the ship was docked between 13 and 15 April.<ref name="Rawlinson-Guardian">{{Cite news |last=Rawlinson |first=Kevin |date=8 May 2026 |title=Third Briton has suspected hantavirus linked to cruise ship outbreak |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/08/third-briton-suspected-hantavirus-cruise-ship-outbreak |access-date=8 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Three dead as virus breaks out on Atlantic cruise ship |url=https://news.sky.com/story/three-dead-as-virus-breaks-out-on-atlantic-cruise-ship-13503266 |website=Sky News |access-date=8 May 2026 }}</ref> This individual was currently hospitalized on the island, and their spouse was isolating.<ref name="kendall-2026b">{{Cite web |last=Kendall |first=Philip |title=Public Notices Regarding the MV Hondius Hantavirus, 6th May 2026 |url=https://www.tristandc.com/government/news-2026-05-06-hantavirus-update.php |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=www.tristandc.com |language=en-GB |ref={{harvid|Kendall|2026b}} }}</ref> The KLM stewardess tested negative for the virus on 8 May.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=KLM-stewardess test negatief op hantavirus |trans-title=KLM flight attendant tests negative for hantavirus |url=https://www.rtl.nl/nieuws/binnenland/artikel/5599168/klm-stewardess-hantavirus-johannesburg |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=RTL.nl |language=nl }}</ref> On this day, GGD Kennemerland announced that everyone on flight KL592 was being monitored and in contact with the GGD, an escalation of the prior risk analysis which only deemed the two rows around the deceased to be at risk.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Secretary of State for Health [[Javier Padilla Bernáldez]] also confirmed that a Spanish passenger on KL592 was symptomatic and hospitalized in [[Alicante]]. The individual sat two rows behind the deceased, and was thus classified as lower risk.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=Última hora del brote de hantavirus, en directo: El Gobierno informa de un caso sospechoso de hantavirus en Alicante |trans-title=Breaking news on the hantavirus outbreak, live: The government reports a suspected case of hantavirus in Alicante |url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2026-05-08/ultima-hora-del-brote-de-hantavirus-en-directo.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=[[El País]] |language=es}}</ref> The US [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] (CDC) classified the outbreak as 'Level 3' emergency response, the lowest on the CDC classification scale. The US administration announced the publication of a full report on the outbreak later that day.<ref name="Watson-ABC">{{Cite web |last1=Watson |first1=Christopher |orig-date=2026-05-08<!--2026-05-08T14:44:26Z per Html--> |title=Hantavirus live updates: CDC classifies outbreak as 'Level 3' emergency response |website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |url=https://abcnews.com/International/live-updates/hantavirus-live-updates-mv-hondius-canary-islands/?id=132746955 |url-status=deviated <!--verified the content at 2026-05-08, 15:06:12; did not verify it hours later when the page changed--> |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508150612/https://abcnews.com/International/live-updates/hantavirus-live-updates-mv-hondius-canary-islands/?id=132746955 |archive-date=8 May 2026 |access-date=8 May 2026 |language=en |last2=Pereira |first2=Ivan |last3=Haworth |first3=Jon |last4=Kekatos |first4=Mary |ref={{harvid|Watson|ABC}} }}</ref>{{better source|date=May 2026 |reason=The Watson-ABC ref is a 'Live update' page which tracks a breaking story and changes content several times a day. It verified the level 3 response for a few hours on 8 May only, before being replaced with other content on the same page. A stable (non-'Live updates') source would be better here.}} In a press conference, the Director of Epidemiology and Environmental Health for [[Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina|Tierra del Fuego]]'s Ministry of Health stated that the patients on the ''Hondius'' were unlikely to have been infected in the province.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Soria |first=Horacio |date=8 May 2026 |title=Argentine authorities say hantavirus patients not likely infected in Tierra del Fuego province |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/argentine-authorities-say-hantavirus-patients-not-likely-infected-tierra-del-2026-05-08/ |access-date=8 May 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref>

Evacuation plans for the arrival of the ship on the [[Canary Islands]] were being finalized. Spain was coordinating the arrival of the ship with 22 countries, and the WHO. Almost all countries were sending evacuation aircraft for their citizens, and the EU provided two aircraft for those who did not have an assigned flight.<ref>{{Cite web|date=8 May 2026 |title=Última hora del brote de hantavirus, en directo: Los ministros de Sanidad e Interior y el director de la OMS viajarán mañana a Tenerife para coordinar la llegada del crucero |url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2026-05-08/ultima-hora-del-brote-de-hantavirus-en-directo.html |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=El País |language=es |ref={{harvid|Pais|2026a}} }}</ref> Countries had differing quarantine plans for their nationals once evacuated.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=Nederlandse opvarenden Hondius gaan zes weken in thuisquarantaine |trans-title=Dutch crew members of the Hondius heading for six weeks of home quarantine |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613635-nederlandse-opvarenden-hondius-gaan-zes-weken-in-thuisquarantaine |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=nos.nl |language=nl}}</ref><ref name="tg vinter jones">{{Cite news |last1=Vinter |first1=Robyn |last2=Jones |first2=Sam |date=8 May 2026 |title=Evacuation of hantavirus-stricken cruise ship could face delays due to bad weather |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/08/spanish-authorities-prepare-arrival-hantavirus-cruise-ship-hondius |access-date=8 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

There had been three deaths, with two confirmed to have been caused by hantavirus.<ref name="WHO-2026a"/> The other one remained under investigation.<ref name="WHO-2026a" /> As of 8 May, the WHO reported two probable cases and six confirmed cases, for a total of eight.<ref name="WHO-2026a" /> The UKHSA reported one additional suspected case, with two Britons being confirmed infected.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=UKHSA update on the hantavirus cruise ship outbreak |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/ukhsa-update-on-the-hantavirus-cruise-ship-outbreak |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=Nederlandse stewardess test negatief op hantavirus, Brit vermoedelijk wel besmet |trans-title=Dutch flight attendant tests negative for hantavirus; British man likely infected |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2613552-nederlandse-stewardess-test-negatief-op-hantavirus-brit-vermoedelijk-wel-besmet |access-date=8 May 2026 |website=NOS |language=nl}}</ref>

The sequences of the virus isolated from a Swiss resident was published on [[virological.org]] on 8 May. The isolate was designated "ANDV/Switzerland/Hu-3337/2026". [[Nextstrain]] pages were set up for this outbreak using these sequences on the same day.<ref name=hu3337>{{cite web |last=Florian |first=Laubscher |title=Complete sequence of Orthohantavirus andesense virus: Swiss resident 2026 |url=https://virological.org/t/complete-sequence-of-orthohantavirus-andesense-virus-swiss-resident-2026/1023 |website=Virological |language=en |date=8 May 2026 |access-date=11 May 2026 |archive-date=12 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512084121/https://virological.org/t/complete-sequence-of-orthohantavirus-andesense-virus-swiss-resident-2026/1023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== <span class="anchor" id="9 May"></span><span class="anchor" id="10 May"></span><span class="anchor" id="9 – 10 May"></span>9–10 May ====
On 9 May, the ship was en route to the Canary Islands and expected to arrive early on 10 May.<ref name="*Vintner-2026*">{{cite news |last1=Robyn |first1=Vintner |date=9 May 2026 |title=UK passengers on hantavirus-hit ship will fly home after Tenerife screening |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/09/hantavirus-ship-hondius-tenerife |access-date=9 May 2026}}</ref>

[[File:The Main Settlement on Tristan da Cunha - Flickr - The Official CTBTO Photostream.jpg|thumb|298x298px|[[Edinburgh of the Seven Seas]], the only settlement on Tristan da Cunha. One inhabitant is suspected of having the virus.]]
On 10 May, British military personnel from the [[16 Air Assault Brigade]] parachuted down to [[Tristan da Cunha]] from a [[Airbus A400M Atlas|RAF A400M Atlas]], where one of its 220 residents, an earlier passenger on the ship, was suspected of having contracted the virus. As the island has no airstrip, parachuting was the only option given the time-sensitive nature of the situation – the nearest port (in South Africa) is over a week sailing time away. In total six paratroopers, a [[Royal Air Force]] (RAF) consultant and an army nurse  arrived to the island while oxygen supplies and medical aid were also dropped.<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 May 2026 |title=British paratroopers land on Tristan da Cunha for suspected hantavirus case |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/10/paratroopers-britain-overseas-territory-suspected-hantavirus-case|access-date=13 May 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB }}</ref> This comes after the island reported their oxygen reserves being at a critical level, ruling out sending equipment by ship from [[Ascension Island]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Lauren |date=10 May 2026 |title=Army parachutes onto Tristan da Cunha to help Briton with suspected hantavirus |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgzv77ldpdo |access-date=10 May 2026 |website=[[BBC News]] |ref={{harvid|Turner|2026a}} |archive-date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260511185608/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgzv77ldpdo |url-status=live }}</ref> 

The ship arrived in the [[Port of Granadilla]], around 05:30 [[Western European Time|WET]] on 10 May and began disembarkation.<ref name="nypost/hondius-in-canary">{{cite news |title=Hantavirus-ridden A flight transporting evacuated passengers landed in Manchester around 21:00 on 10 May. The passengers—consisting of twenty UK citizens, one German national residing in the UK, and one Japanese man (who was evacuated at Japan's request)—were hospitalized at [[Arrowe Park Hospital]], the location of UK's initial quarantine during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Rawlinson-2026">{{Cite news |last=Rawlinson |first=Kevin |date=11 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus cruise ship passengers enter isolation facility after evacuation to UK |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/11/mv-hondius-passengers-from-hantavirus-cruise-ship-enter-isolation-facility-in-wirral |access-date=11 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

==== <span class="anchor" id="11 – 12 May"></span>11 May ====
It was announced that the symptomatic French national had tested positive, with her health worsening overnight. Additionally, one asymptomatic American tested positive, and another had mild symptoms.<ref name="Funk-2026">{{Cite web |last1=Funk |first1=Josh |last2=Corder |first2=Mike |date=11 May 2026 |title=3 passengers, French and American, test positive or have symptoms of hantavirus after evacuation |url=https://apnews.com/article/hantavirus-outbreak-hondius-cruise-ship-df0e7e1fb9c7fd3e4092be06e684f644 |access-date=11 May 2026 |website=AP News |language=en |archive-date=14 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260514083820/https://apnews.com/article/hantavirus-outbreak-hondius-cruise-ship-df0e7e1fb9c7fd3e4092be06e684f644 |url-status=live }}</ref> The French government increased its public health alertness level, and had identified 22 French nationals who were high risk contact cases with infected individuals.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Battaglia |first=Mattea |date=11 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus : après la découverte d'un premier cas positif en France, le gouvernement entend « briser les chaînes » de transmission du virus |trans-title=Hantavirus: after the discovery of the first confirmed case in France, the government intends to 'break the chain' of transmission |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/planete/article/2026/05/11/hantavirus-comment-le-gouvernement-entend-briser-les-chaines-de-transmission-du-virus_6687870_3244.html |access-date=11 May 2026 |work=Le Monde |language=FR}}</ref> Later, the WHO reported that the woman was in "very critical condition", and that she had already shown symptoms while on the ship. In the evening of 11 May local time, one of the Spanish nationals who had arrived in Spain the day before tested positive. The 13 other Spanish nationals tested negative.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-12 |title=Última hora del brote de hantavirus, en directo {{!}} Ya son 10 los casos registrados (incluidos los tres fallecidos), tras confirmarse el del español contagiado |trans-title=Breaking news on the hantavirus outbreak, live {{!}} There are now 10 confirmed cases (including the three deaths), following the confirmation of the case of the infected Spaniard |url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2026-05-12/ultima-hora-del-brote-de-hantavirus-en-directo.html |website=El País |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260513090934/https://elpais.com/sociedad/2026-05-12/ultima-hora-del-brote-de-hantavirus-en-directo.html |archive-date=13 May 2026 |access-date=2026-05-13 }}</ref>

total, 122 individuals disembarked the ship in Tenerife and were repatriated to their home countries, or the Netherlands for those nationalities that did not provide their own evacuation flights.<ref name="Oceanwide-2026b" />

==== 12 May ====
A Spanish passenger was confirmed positive, exhibiting symptoms, and was isolated in hospital. 

Twelve hospital workers at the Radboud University Medical Center in [[Nijmegen]], Netherlands, failed to comply with protocols and were placed in isolation. The hospital staff followed standard protocols rather than strict protocols while drawing the patient's blood during admission on 7 May, and did not follow appropriate safety protocols when draining the patient's urine on 9 May.<ref name="Radboudumc"/><ref name="Voskamp-12May">{{cite web |last1=Voskamp |first1=Elena |title=Twelve Radboudumc employees in quarantine after hantavirus protocol error |url=https://dutchtimes.nl/news/netherlands/twelve-radboudumc-employees-in-quarantine-after-hantavirus-protocol-error/ |website=Dutch Times |access-date=23 June 2026 |date=12 May 2026}}</ref>

==== 13 May ====
Since the hospitalization of the French passenger on 10 May, her condition has worsened. On 13 May, French authorities stated that she is on life-support. They also said that this is "the final stage of supportive care".<ref name="Iribarren-2026">{{Cite web |last=Iribarren |first=Marta Iraola |date=13 May 2026 |title=Are hantavirus cases spreading? French woman in critical condition in hospital |url=https://www.euronews.com/health/2026/05/13/are-hantavirus-cases-spreading-french-woman-in-critical-condition-in-hospital |access-date=13 May 2026 |website=Euronews |archive-date=14 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260514013121/https://www.euronews.com/health/2026/05/13/are-hantavirus-cases-spreading-french-woman-in-critical-condition-in-hospital |url-status=live }}</ref> That same day, the WHO posted its third official update regarding the outbreak, and adjusted one of the previously confirmed cases to inconclusive after a second test came back negative, awaiting a third test from the American national who had shown no symptoms.<ref name=WHO-don601>{{Cite web |title=Hantavirus cluster linked to cruise ship travel, Multi-country |url=https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON601 |date=2026-05-13 |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=World Health Organization |language=en |archive-date=15 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260515130354/https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON601 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 15 May ====
On 15 May, the CDC announced that an American passenger who had developed flu-like symptoms on board and who had initially been listed as having "inconclusive" test results was retested with negative result and showed no antibodies, meaning he was never infected.<ref name="Stump-2026" />

A Canadian passenger isolating in British Columbia tested "presumptively positive", with the patient hospitalized and three others under medical observation. While awaiting national laboratory confirmation, health officials are treating the case as positive during the 21-day isolation period.<ref name="Schmunk-16 May" />

==== 18 May ====
[[File:Z9 & HONDIUS (55277179657).jpg|thumb|The ''Hondius'' arriving in Rotterdam. On the left is a tour boat from where the press could follow the arrival.]]
On 18 May, MV ''Hondius'' docked in Rotterdam. Disinfection of the vessel began, and is estimated to take 3 to 4 days. Five crew members, including the captain, will stay on board during the disinfection.<ref name="Oceanwide-18May">{{Cite press release |title=Press update m/v Hondius: 18 May 2026 |url=https://oceanwide-expeditions.com/press/press-update-m-v-hondius-18-may-2026-18-30-hrs-cet |access-date=18 May 2026 |website=[[Oceanwide Expeditions]] |language=en }}</ref> The remaining on-board were tested again and disembarked. Of those, the two Dutch medical workers went home, where they would self-quarantine. The 20 non-Dutch crew (17 from the Philippines and 3 from Ukraine) entered into quarantine for six weeks in separate cabins. The body of the deceased German woman was taken off board to be cremated in the Netherlands.<ref name="Oceanwide-18May" /><ref name="Van Campenhout-17May">{{cite news |last1=Van Campenhout |first1=Charlotte |date=17 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus-hit liner reaches Rotterdam, crew being quarantined and ship disinfected |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/hantavirus-hit-cruise-ship-due-arrive-rotterdam-port-final-destination-2026-05-18/ |access-date=18 May 2026}}</ref> The status of the Canadian passenger was updated by the national lab and "confirmed" positive.<ref name="Joannou-18 May">{{cite news |last1=Joannou |first1=Ashley |date=18 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus case confirmed on Vancouver Island by national lab test |work=[[Times Colonist]] |url=https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/hantavirus-case-confirmed-on-vancouver-island-by-national-lab-test-12294655 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260519015611/https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/hantavirus-case-confirmed-on-vancouver-island-by-national-lab-test-12294655 |archive-date=19 May 2026 |access-date=19 May 2026}}</ref>

==== 22 May ====
A crew member already in isolation in the Netherlands tested positive, raising the total number of cases to twelve, including the three deaths. No deaths have been reported since 2 May.<ref name="Burke-22May">{{cite news |last1=Burke |first1=Minyvonne |date=22 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus cases linked to cruise ship rise to 12 after crew member tests positive |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/hantavirus-cases-linked-cruise-ship-rise-12-crew-member-tests-positive-rcna346481 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260522222327/https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/hantavirus-cases-linked-cruise-ship-rise-12-crew-member-tests-positive-rcna346481 |archive-date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref>

The [[Royal Navy]] ship [[HMS Medway (P223)|HMS ''Medway'']] arrives at Tristan da Cunha, bringing additional medical supplies and a civilian medical team to replace the military medical team who had parachuted onto the island on 10 May.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=Tom |title=Navy sends doctors to treat rat virus patient on remote island |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2026/05/24/navy-sends-doctors-rat-virus-patient-tristan-da-cunha/ |website=The Telegraph |access-date=5 June 2026 |date=24 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=HMS Medway arrives at Tristan da Cunha with medics and supplies |website=Navy Lookout |url=https://www.navylookout.com/hms-medway-arrives-at-tristan-da-cunha-with-medics-and-supplies/ |access-date=5 June 2026 |date=23 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kendall |first1=Philip |title=Hantavirus - The Next Steps, 23rd May 2026 |url=https://www.tristandc.com/news-2026-05-23-hantavirus-update.php |publisher=Tristan da Cunha Government |access-date=5 June 2026 |date=23 May 2026}}</ref>

==== 24 May ====
A Spanish national who was evacuated from the ship tests positive while quarantining in the [[Gómez Ulla Military Hospital]]. After testing positive, the patient was transferred to an isolation unit.<ref name="Faus-25May"/>

HMS ''Medway'' departs Tristan da Cunha, extracting the military medics and paratoopers who had parachuted onto the island on 10 May.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kendall |first1=Philip |title=HMS Medway Departs after Successfully Exchanging Personnel |url=https://www.tristandc.com/news-2026-05-24-hms-medway.php |publisher=Tristan da Cunha Government |access-date=5 June 2026 |date=24 May 2026}}</ref>

==== 28 May ====
The patient with hantavirus who was hospitalized at [[Leiden University Medical Center]] in the Netherlands is discharged.<ref>{{cite web |title=Admitted patient with hantavirus has left the LUMC |url=https://www.lumc.nl/en/news/2026/lumc-receives-patient-with-possible-hantavirus-infection/ |website=Leiden University Medical Center |access-date=19 July 2026 |date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

==== 30 May ====
After undergoing deep cleaning, MV ''Hondius'' is cleared by the [[Municipal Health Service]] (the Dutch health authority) to return to service. The ship is scheduled to depart Rotterdam on 6 June en route to [[Svalbard]] for resumption of service on 13 June.<ref name="Oceanwide-1 June"/><ref name="Wilson-1 June"/>

=== June ===
==== 3 June ====
It is reported that one of the Radboud University Medical Center employees, who was placed in isolation after not observing proper safety protocols during the treatment of a hantavirus patient, tested weakly positive for hantavirus. The employee was not symptomatic, and subsequent tests were negative. The [[National Institute for Public Health and the Environment]] and Radboud University Medical Center do not consider the employee to be a positive case, as the subsequent negative tests and lack of symptoms are not consistent with a hantavirus infection.<ref name="Mudde-3June"/><ref name="Radboudumc">{{cite web |title=Radboudumc vangt patiënt op met mogelijke hantavirus-besmetting - Update 22 juni, 13.00 uur |url=https://www.radboudumc.nl/nieuws/2026/radboudumc-vangt-patient-op-met-mogelijke-hantavirusbesmetting |publisher=Radboud University Medical Center |access-date=23 June 2026 |language=nl |date=22 June 2026}}</ref>

==== 5 June ====
The private yacht ''Titaina Explorer'' departs from [[Pitcairn Island]] (a remote [[British Overseas Territory]]) for [[Easter Island]], evacuating an asymptomatic American woman who had travelled on the MV ''Hondius''. The woman had travelled from the United States to [[Tahiti]] on 7 May, then travelled to Pitcairn Island, where she had been isolating. Pitcairn Island is a remote island with no airport and infrequent maritime services, so the United States spent $750,000 to charter the private yacht to transport the woman to Easter Island — Easter Island has flights to [[Santiago]], from where the woman could then be transported to the United States for treatment if necessary. Due to the woman not disclosing her exposure to the virus when she travelled through Tahiti on the way to Pitcairn Island, [[French Polynesian]] authorities refused to allow the woman to transit through Tahiti, causing delays in finding a way to evacuate the woman to the United States.<ref name="Copeland-13May">{{cite web |last1=Copeland |first1=Thomas |date=13 May 2026 |title=Woman isolating on British island in South Pacific after hantavirus contact |work=[[BBC]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx21p7k70reo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260513182008/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx21p7k70reo |archive-date=13 May 2026 |access-date=19 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="Lee-12June">{{cite web |last1=Lee |first1=Matthew |title=US puts up $750K to evacuate an American who was aboard hantavirus cruise ship from remote island |url=https://apnews.com/article/hantavirus-ship-evacuation-american-yacht-33ba5ddb8374d0083271669e7ba52b04 |website=AP News |access-date=12 June 2026 |language=en |date=11 June 2026}}</ref>

==== 9 June ====
It is reported that the patient who was hospitalized in [[British Columbia]], Canada was discharged towards the end of the previous week.<ref name="Sousa-9 June"/>

==== 10 June ====
The patient hospitalized on Tristan da Cunha tests positive for the virus.<ref name="Lu-11June"/>

=== July ===
==== 2 July ====
The last identified close contact of a person exposed to the virus completes quarantine. As a result, the World Health Organization declares the outbreak to be over.<ref name="Guardian-2 July"/>

==== 3 July ====
The civilian medical team sent to Tristan da Cunha from the [[Falkland Islands]] to assist in treating a patient with a hantavirus infection departs on the MFV ''Edinburgh''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kendall |first1=Philip |last2=Green |first2=Kelly |title=Postscript to the Hantavirus Outbreak |url=https://www.tristandc.com/news-2026-07-09-hantavirus-postscript.php |publisher=Tristan da Cunha Government & Tristan da Cunha Association |access-date=19 July 2026 |date=9 July 2026}}</ref>

=== August ===
==== 6 August ====
The French woman who had been hospitalized in a Paris intensive care unit with a hantavirus infection is discharged after 3 months in hospital.<ref name="Le Monde-August">{{cite news |title=Hantavirus: Tourist who transited France in July tests positive |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/health/article/2026/08/06/hantavirus-tourist-who-transited-france-in-july-tests-positive_6756228_14.html |access-date=8 August 2026 |work=Le Monde |date=6 August 2026}}</ref>

== On board health care and monitoring ==
The ''Hondius'' is equipped with a cabin for the ship's doctor, normally only one,<ref name="overheid.nl" /> and an infirmary.<ref name="Ajay-2017">{{cite web |author=Ajay |date=22 December 2017 |title=Hondius Polar Expedition Ship |website=Ship Technology |url=https://www.ship-technology.com/projects/hondius-polar-expedition-ship/?cf-view&cf-closed |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--no byline--> |date=6 May 2026 |title=MV Hondius {{!}} Ice-Class Expedition Ship |publisher=Arctos Travel |location=Longyearbyen, Norway |orig-date=2026-02-05 |url=https://arctostravel.com/expedition-ships/hondius |archive-url= |archive-date= |at=Onboard services |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref> It is intended more for the minor health problems typically arising at sea, and stocks [[anti-inflammatory drugs]], some [[Over-the-counter drug|over-the-counter medications]], and [[Oxygen tank|oxygen tanks]]. It lacks the kind of sophisticated equipment such as scanners or ventilators needed to diagnose or treat serious [[respiratory illness]].<ref name="Wu-2026">{{cite magazine |last1=Wu |first1=Katherine J. |date=7 May 2026 |title=What Happened on the Hantavirus Cruise, According to a Doctor on Board |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/health/2026/05/hantavirus-cruise-doctor/687095/ |access-date=8 May 2026 |magazine=[[The Atlantic]] |publisher=The Atlantic |location=Washington, D.C.|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

By the end of April, the ship's doctor was among the two crew members who were very ill and confined to quarters. On 1 May, one of the passengers, who is a doctor, began rendering medical assistance to other passengers and crew. As the situation escalated, he also provided health care information resources for passengers on board, as well as became the central point of contact on board for health authorities.<ref name="Wu-2026" /><ref name="Goodman-19May">{{cite web |last1=Goodman |first1=Brenda |last2=Hoffman |first2= Francesca Giuliani |date=19 May 2026 |title=American passenger on hantavirus-hit cruise feels 'blindsided,' 'misled' by new quarantine orders |work=KSL |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51500025/american-passenger-on-hantavirus-hit-cruise-feels-blindsided-misled-by-new-quarantine-orders |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260522063608/https://www.ksl.com/article/51500025/american-passenger-on-hantavirus-hit-cruise-feels-blindsided-misled-by-new-quarantine-orders |archive-date=22 May 2026 |access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref> While docked outside [[Cape Verde]], two doctors and one nurse made three trips to the ship to provide additional care to passengers.<ref name="ap_cape">{{cite news |last1=Imray |first1=Gerald |title=A cruise ship is waiting for help after 3 people died in a suspected hantavirus outbreak |url=https://apnews.com/article/hantavirus-cruise-ship-hondius-cape-verde-74c38cab57da78f7d4c0eefac4311edf |access-date=11 May 2026 |work=[[AP News]] |date=4 May 2026 |language=en |archive-date=12 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512021912/https://apnews.com/article/hantavirus-cruise-ship-hondius-cape-verde-74c38cab57da78f7d4c0eefac4311edf |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 May, four medical experts embarked while the ship was leaving Cape Verde. Two of these were medical specialists from [[Amsterdam University Medical Center]] and {{interlanguage link|Central Military Hospital|nl|Centraal Militair Hospitaal}} in [[Utrecht]]. The two others were epidemiologists from Italy and the Netherlands, meant to investigate the scope of the virus on the ship.<ref name="oceanwide 8may" /> The selection, transport and coordination of these experts was assisted by the WHO and [[European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control]].<ref name="overheid.nl" />

== International response ==
The [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) issued guidance aimed at port facilities and health authorities and agencies handling the disembarkation and monitoring of individuals on the MV ''Hondius''.<ref name="WHO-Tech Note">{{cite web |author=[[WHO]] |date=10 May 2026 |title=WHO Technical note for the disembarkation and onward management of passengers and crew in the context of an Andes virus-associated cluster MV Hondius cruise ship |orig-date=8 May 2026 |website=WHO |url=https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-technical-note-for-the-disembarkation-and-onward-management-of-passengers-and-crew-in-the-context-of-an-andes-virus-associated-cluster-mv-hondius-cruise-ship <!--download-url=https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/coronaviruse/situation-reports/who-technical-note-for-the-disembarkation-and-onward-management-of-passengers-and-crew-in-the-context-of-an-andes-virus-associated-cluster-mv-hondius-cruise-ship.pdf?sfvrsn=56272a28_3&download=true--> |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260510205017/https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/who-technical-note-for-the-disembarkation-and-onward-management-of-passengers-and-crew-in-the-context-of-an-andes-virus-associated-cluster-mv-hondius-cruise-ship |archive-date=10 May 2026 |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref>

=== Passenger monitoring and contact tracing ===
The WHO has been coordinating monitoring of those who disembarked or were evacuated with health care agencies in twelve countries, including Canada, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand, [[Saint Kitts and Nevis]], Singapore, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, the United Kingdom, and the United States.<ref name="McArthur-2026">{{cite news |last=McArthur |first=Tom |date=8 May 2026 |title=Worldwide race to trace passengers from hantavirus-hit cruise ship |work=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyp1505p84o |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508154501/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyp1505p84o |archive-date=8 May 2026 |access-date=8 May 2026}}</ref>

=== Canary Islands arrival ===
On 6 May, the ship was anchored near Cape Verde, which was not considered able to handle the scale of operation needed for the ship's safe evacuation.<ref name="aikman-2026" /> Instead, it intended to travel to [[Tenerife]] and have its passengers disembark there. However president of the Canary Islands [[Fernando Clavijo (politician)|Fernando Clavijo]] said he "cannot allow [''Hondius''] to enter the Canaries" and refused to receive the ship in Tenerife.<ref name="aikman-2026" /><ref name="the-independent-2026" /> Clavijo's refusal stemmed from his concern that the ship's arrival would endanger the people of the Canary Islands, a view shared by many islanders, particularly in light of [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Canary Islands|their experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="the-independent-2026" /> The cruise company said that "Spain has a moral and legal obligation to assist these people, among whom are several Spanish citizens".<ref name="aikman-2026" />

Despite the objections of the Canary Islands' president, Spain approved the plan for the ''Hondius'' to dock in Tenerife, with its health agency stating it was "in accordance with international law and humanitarian principles".<ref name="grierson-2026a" /> The ship set sail for the islands on 6 May.<ref name="grierson-2026a" /><ref>{{Cite news |title=Hantavirus-hit cruise ship leaves for Tenerife after three people are evacuated |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/world/2026/05/05/human-to-human-transmission-suspected-on-hantavirus-cruise-ship/ |access-date=7 May 2026 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] |language=en }}</ref>

=== Rodent investigation ===
The index case couple had been traveling through Argentina prior to boarding the MV ''Hondius'', leading experts to believe the couple may have contracted the virus in the country. Argentinian officials initially believed that the couple may have contracted the virus in [[Ushaia]] in the [[Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina|Tierra del Fuego Province]] — the same city that the MV ''Hondius'' departed from — while visiting a landfill for birdwatching. Hantavirus had never been detected in the [[Tierra del Fuego]] archipelago before.<ref name="Zibell-10 May">{{cite web |last1=Zibell |first1=Matías |title=Argentinian tourism hotspot denies causing hantavirus outbreak |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx21ej471g2o |website=BBC |access-date=2 July 2026 |date=10 May 2026}}</ref>

From 18 to 22 May, Argentine scientists from the [[Malbrán Institute]] trapped and tested rodents for hantavirus in the forests around Ushuaia.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Debre |first1=Isabel |title=Argentines hunting for source of hantavirus outbreak trap rodents in southernmost city |url=https://apnews.com/article/argentina-hantavirus-investigation-cruise-ship-hondius-outbreak-ushuaia-6e02980f2ab1637e3ceeddc7d1429b5f |website=AP News |access-date=2 July 2026 |language=en |date=19 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="Buenos Aires Times">{{cite web |title=Experts: Hantavirus detected in Tierra del Fuego, but no link to cruise outbreak |url=https://www.batimes.com.ar/news/argentina/experts-hantavirus-detected-in-tierra-del-fuego-but-no-link-to-cruise-outbreak.phtml |website=Buenos Aires Times |access-date=2 July 2026 |language=en |date=29 June 2026}}</ref> From 8 to 12 June, a team of scientists from the Malbrán Institute, working with scientists from the United States' [[Centers for Disease Control]], trapped and tested rodents in [[Malargüe]] in the [[Mendoza Province]] for hantavirus, a city that had been visited by the deceased couple.<ref>{{cite web |first=Isabel |last=Debre |title=Argentina expands hantavirus probe, sending teams to trap and test rats in Mendoza |url=https://apnews.com/article/argentina-hantavirus-investigation-cdc-ushuaia-mendoza-1e375f0eb2120343bfde222bc47d53c5 |website=AP News |access-date=2 July 2026 |language=en |date=5 June 2026}}</ref> No ''[[Oligoryzomys longicaudatus]]'' specimens — the species considered the primary reservoir of the Andes virus — were captured in either location.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Viveros |first1=Rocío |title=Studies in Mendoza and Tierra del Fuego rule out that the hantavirus outbreak on the cruise was caused by rodents |url=https://noticiasambientales.com/science/studies-in-mendoza-and-tierra-del-fuego-rule-out-that-the-hantavirus-outbreak-on-the-cruise-was-caused-by-rodents/ |website=Noticias Ambientales |access-date=2 July 2026 |date=16 June 2026}}</ref>

Hantavirus was detected in 5 of the 144 rodents captured near Ushuaia, and was determined to be a previously undescribed viral variant related to the Andes virus; however, it was a different variant of the virus to the one that spread on the MV ''Hondius''.<ref name="Buenos Aires Times"/> Prior to this investigation, hantavirus had never been detected in the [[Tierra del Fuego]] archipelago.<ref name="Zibell-10 May"/>

== Misinformation and disinformation ==
Several conspiracy theories emerged online following the outbreak. Some made the false claim that the outbreak was caused by Israel, and that the name of the virus is derived from the Hebrew word for ''scam'' or ''fake'' ([[hantavirus]] takes its name from the [[Hantan River]] in Korea).<ref name="Euro News 2026" /> Other false claims portray the hantavirus outbreak as a side-effect of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Rosenbluth |first=Teddy |last2=Myers |first2=Steven Lee |date=2026-05-12 |title=The Hantavirus Outbreak Is Resurrecting Covid-Era Misinformation Tactics |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/well/hantavirus-covid-misinformation.html |access-date=2026-05-18 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=15 May 2026 |title=Fact Check: Hantavirus infection is not a confirmed side effect of Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine |url=https://www.reuters.com/fact-check/hantavirus-infection-is-not-confirmed-side-effect-pfizers-covid-19-vaccine-2026-05-08/ |access-date=18 May 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> and as a scheme by pharmaceutical companies to sell vaccines, citing [[Moderna]]'s development of a [[hantavirus vaccine]] in 2024.<ref name="Euro News 2026">{{cite web |title=From 'staged' to Israel: Hantavirus misinformation runs rampant online |url=https://www.euronews.com/video/2026/05/13/staged-claims-and-israeli-hoaxes-debunking-viral-conspiracy-theories-about-hantavirus |website=Euro News |access-date=18 May 2026}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Rigby |first=Jennifer |date=14 May 2026 |title=Hantavirus outbreak tests post-COVID health communications playbook |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/hantavirus-outbreak-tests-post-covid-health-communications-playbook-2026-05-15/ |access-date=18 May 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Several [[AI-generated]] images with false information about the outbreak have circulated on social media.<ref name=":0" /> Unsupported claims that [[Ivermectin]] can cure hantavirus were endorsed by [[Far-right politics|far-right]] former US Congress member [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]].<ref name="Euro News 2026" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldhamer |first=Marisha |date=May 8, 2026 |title=Ivermectin is not a proven treatment for hantavirus |url=https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.B2AR3WF |access-date=May 18, 2026 |website=[[AFP Fact Check]]}}</ref>

The [[World Health Organization]] addressed the misinformation regarding the outbreak in Q&A sessions on social media.<ref name=":1" />

== Legacy and impact ==

=== Impetus for further study ===
There is little evidence about how hantavirus is transmitted because outbreaks are rare and mostly limited to Latin America. The Andes strain is the only one which can spread person-to-person, and little is known about it; no vaccine is available.<ref name="Cullinan-21May">{{cite news |last1=Cullinan |first1=Maeve |date=21 May 2026 |title=Scientists to monitor British cruise passengers in hantavirus study |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/global-health/science-and-disease/scientists-to-monitor-british-cruise-hantavirus-passengers/
<!--no archive--> |access-date=23 May 2026}}</ref>

The [[UK Health Security Agency]] (UKHSA) is planning a study to learn more about Andes virus based on the cruise ship outbreak. Twenty British nationals who were on board and potentially exposed to the virus have volunteered to participate. None of the Britons isolating in the UK tested positive.<ref name="Cullinan-21May" />

The UKHSA study is being run by the [[International Severe Acute Respiratory and Emergency Infection Consortium]] (ISARIC), known for gathering evidence about infectious diseases. It seeks evidence about how and when individuals become infectious and for how long; who gets sick, the progression of the disease, and what the risk factors are. A key question is whether individuals can become infected without having symptoms, as this would impact how health agencies monitor the disease and implement contact-tracing.<ref name="Cullinan-21May" />

'''<!--Definition and symptoms-->Malaria''' is a [[Mosquito-borne disease|mosquito-borne infectious disease]] that is transmitted by the bite of ''[[Anopheles]]'' [[mosquito]]es.<ref name="WHO-Vector-2023">{{cite web |title=Vector-borne diseases |url=https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/vector-borne-diseases |access-date=24 April 2022 |publisher=[[World Health Organization]] |archive-date=4 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104001515/https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/vector-borne-diseases |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> The [[Signs and symptoms|symptoms]] of human malaria typically include [[fever]], [[Fatigue (medical)|fatigue]], [[vomiting]] and [[headache]]s.<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Basu S, Sahi PK | title=Malaria: An Update | journal=Indian Journal of Pediatrics | volume=84 | issue=7 | pages=521–528 | date=July 2017 | pmid=28357581 | doi=10.1007/s12098-017-2332-2 }}</ref> In severe cases, the disease can cause [[jaundice]], [[Epileptic seizure|seizures]], [[coma]], or [[death]].<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Fact sheet about malaria |url=https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/malaria |access-date=10 May 2024 |publisher=World Health Organization |archive-date=2 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502021814/https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/malaria |url-status=live}}</ref> Symptoms usually begin 10 to 15 days after being bitten by an infected [[Anopheles mosquito|''Anopheles'' mosquito]].<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /><ref name="CDC-FAQ-2023">{{cite web | url=https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/about/faqs.html | title=CDC - Malaria - FAQs | date=28 June 2023 | access-date=9 September 2017 | archive-date=13 May 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513112631/http://www.cdc.gov/malaria/about/faqs.html | url-status=live}}</ref> Those who survive an infection may develop partial [[Immunity (medicine)|immunity]], being susceptible to reinfection although with milder symptoms.<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /> This partial [[Immunity (medical)|resistance]] disappears over months to years if the person has no continuing exposure to malaria.<ref name="Caraballo-2014">{{cite journal |vauthors=Caraballo H, King K |title=Emergency department management of mosquito-borne illness: malaria, dengue and West Nile virus |journal=Emergency Medicine Practice |volume=16 |issue=5 |pages=1–23; quiz 23–24 |date=May 2014 |pmid=25207355 |url=http://www.ebmedicine.net/topics.php?paction=showTopic&topic_id=405 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160801202316/http://www.ebmedicine.net/topics.php?paction=showTopic&topic_id=405 |archive-date=1 August 2016}}</ref>

<!-- Cause and diagnosis -->Malaria is caused by single-celled [[Parasitism|parasites]] of the genus ''[[Plasmodium]],''<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> generally spread through the bites of an infected female ''Anopheles'' mosquito.<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Walter K, John CC | title=Malaria | journal=JAMA | volume=327 | issue=6 | page=597 | date=February 2022 | pmid=35133414 | doi=10.1001/jama.2021.21468 | doi-access=free| hdl=1805/37679 | hdl-access=free }}</ref> The mosquito bite introduces the parasites from the mosquito's [[saliva]] into the blood.<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> The parasites initially reproduce and mature in the [[liver]] without causing symptoms.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lifecycle of the malaria parasite |url=https://www.mmv.org/malaria/about-malaria/lifecycle-malaria-parasite |access-date=8 January 2026 |website=Medicines for Malaria Venture |language=en |archive-date=2 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260102114122/https://www.mmv.org/malaria/about-malaria/lifecycle-malaria-parasite |url-status=live }}</ref> After a few days the mature parasites spread into the bloodstream, where they infect and destroy [[Red blood cell|red blood cells]], causing the symptoms of infection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Malaria factsheet |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/malaria-prevention-transmission-symptoms/malaria-transmission-incubation-period-symptoms |access-date=8 January 2026 |website=Public Health England |language=en |archive-date=1 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901042339/https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/malaria-prevention-transmission-symptoms/malaria-transmission-incubation-period-symptoms |url-status=live }}</ref> Five species of ''Plasmodium'' commonly infect humans.<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> The three species associated with more severe cases are ''[[Plasmodium falciparum|P.&nbsp;falciparum]]'' (which is responsible for the vast majority of malaria deaths), ''[[Plasmodium vivax|P.&nbsp;vivax]]'' and ''[[Plasmodium knowlesi|P.&nbsp;knowlesi]]'' (a [[simian]] malaria that spills over into thousands of people a year).<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /><ref>{{cite web |last=World Health Organization |title=Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016-2030 |url=https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/documents/global-technical-strategy-for-malaria-2016-2030.pdf |access-date=19 February 2024 |archive-date=22 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240222024003/https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/documents/global-technical-strategy-for-malaria-2016-2030.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Plasmodium ovale|P.&nbsp;ovale]]'' and ''[[Plasmodium malariae|P.&nbsp;malariae]]'' generally cause a milder form of malaria.<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /><ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> Malaria is typically diagnosed by the [[histology|microscopic examination]] of blood using [[blood film]]s, or with [[Malaria antigen detection tests|antigen-based]] [[rapid diagnostic test]]s.<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /> Methods that use the [[polymerase chain reaction]] to detect the parasite's [[DNA]] have been developed, and are now considered the gold standard, but they are not widely available or used in areas where malaria is common, due to their cost and complexity.<ref name="Nadjm-2012">{{cite journal | vauthors=Nadjm B, Behrens RH | title=Malaria: an update for physicians | journal=Infectious Disease Clinics of North America | volume=26 | issue=2 | pages=243–259 | date=June 2012 | pmid=22632637 | doi=10.1016/j.idc.2012.03.010}}</ref>

<!-- Prevention and treatment -->The risk of disease can be reduced by preventing mosquito bites through the use of [[mosquito net]]s and [[insect repellent]]s or with [[Mosquito control|mosquito-control measures]] such as spraying [[insecticide]]s and draining [[standing water]].<ref name="Caraballo-2014" /> Several [[Preventive healthcare|prophylactic]] medications are available to [[malaria prophylaxis|prevent malaria]] in areas where the disease is common.<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> As of 2023, two [[malaria vaccine]]s have been endorsed by the [[World Health Organization]].<ref name="WHO recommends R21-2023">{{cite web |title=WHO recommends R21/Matrix-M vaccine for malaria prevention in updated advice on immunization |url=https://www.who.int/news/item/02-10-2023-who-recommends-r21-matrix-m-vaccine-for-malaria-prevention-in-updated-advice-on-immunization |access-date=8 December 2023 |date=2 October 2023 |archive-date=3 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003232601/https://www.who.int/news/item/02-10-2023-who-recommends-r21-matrix-m-vaccine-for-malaria-prevention-in-updated-advice-on-immunization |url-status=live}}</ref> The parasites have evolved resistance to several [[antimalarial medication]]s; for example, [[chloroquine]]-resistant ''P.&nbsp;falciparum'' has spread to most malaria-prone areas and resistance to artemisinin has become a problem in some parts of [[Southeast Asia]].<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> Because of this, drug treatment for malaria infection should be tailored to best fit the [[List of Plasmodium species|''Plasmodium'' species]] involved and the geographical location where the infection was acquired.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2025 |title=Treatment of Uncomplicated Malaria |url=https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/hcp/clinical-guidance/treatment-uncomplicated.html |access-date=8 January 2026 |website=Centers for Disease Control and Treatment |language=en-us}}</ref> 

<!-- Epidemiology and history -->The disease is widespread in the [[Tropics|tropical]] and [[subtropical]] regions that exist in a broad band around the [[equator]].<ref>{{cite book | vauthors=Baiden F, Malm KL, Binka F |chapter=Malaria | veditors=Detels R, Karim QA, Baum F, Li L, Leyland AH |title=Oxford Textbook of Global Public Health |date=2021 |pages=227–248 |isbn=978-0-19-881680-5 |doi=10.1093/med/9780198816805.003.0073 |edition=7th}}</ref><ref name="Caraballo-2014" /> This includes much of [[sub-Saharan Africa]], [[Asia]] and [[Latin America]].<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" /> In 2024, some 282 million cases of malaria worldwide resulted in an estimated 610,000 deaths, up from 273 million cases in 2023.<ref name="WHO-Report-2025a" /> The WHO African Region accounted approximately 94% of global malaria cases and 95% of total deaths occurred in 2024.<ref name="WHO-Report-2025a" /><ref name="WHO-Briefing-2024">{{Cite web |title=Current state: The malaria situation worldwide |url=https://worldmalariareport2024.org/ |access-date=6 January 2026 |website=WHO: World Malaria Report Global Briefing Kit 2024 |language=en}}</ref> 

Malaria is commonly associated with [[poverty]] and has a significant negative effect on economic development;<ref name="Gollin-2007" /><ref name="Worrall-2005" /> in 2005 it was estimated that [[Africa]] loses US$12 billion a year due to increased healthcare costs, lost ability to work and adverse effects on [[tourism]].<ref name="Greenwood-2005" />

[[File:En.Wikipedia-VideoWiki-Malaria.webm|thumb|thumbtime=0:02|upright=1.3|Video summary ([[Wikipedia:VideoWiki/Malaria|script]])]]
{{TOC level|3}}

== Etymology ==
The word ''malaria'' originates from [[Middle Ages|Medieval]] {{langx|it|mala aria}}, 'bad air', a part of [[miasma theory]]; the disease was formerly called ''ague, paludism'' or ''marsh fever'' due to its association with swamps and marshland.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Reiter P | title=From Shakespeare to Defoe: malaria in England in the Little Ice Age | journal=Emerging Infectious Diseases | volume=6 | issue=1 | pages=1–11 | date=1999 | pmid=10653562 | pmc=2627969 | doi=10.3201/eid0601.000101}}</ref> The word appeared in English at least as early as 1768.<ref>{{cite book |vauthors=Sharpe S |date=1768 |title=A view of the customs, manners, drama, &c. of Italy, as they are described in the Frusta letteraria; and in the Account of Italy in English, written by Mr. Baretti; compared with the Letters from Italy, written by Mr. Sharp |location=London |publisher=W. Nicoll}}</ref> The scientific study of malaria is malariology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Definition of MALARIOLOGY |website=Merriam-Webster Dictionary |url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/malariology |language=en |access-date=19 November 2024 |archive-date=2 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250802160413/https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/malariology |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Signs and symptoms==
[[File:Symptoms of Malaria.png|thumb|upright=1.15|Main symptoms of malaria<ref name="Fairhurst-2015" />]]

Symptoms during the early stages of malaria infection are fever, chills, headache, nausea and vomiting and diarrhoea; more serious cases may show enlarged [[Splenomegaly|spleen]] or [[Hepatomegaly|liver]] and mild [[jaundice]].<ref name="Crutcher-1996" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=12 March 2024 |title=Symptoms of Malaria |url=https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/symptoms/index.html |access-date=16 January 2026 |website=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention |language=en-us}}</ref> These symptoms can resemble other conditions such as [[sepsis]], [[gastroenteritis]], [[Influenza|flu]] and other [[viral disease]]s.<ref name="Nadjm-2012" /><ref name="Bartoloni-2012" /> Without treatment, symptoms - particularly the fever - can settle into a regular pattern, recurring every two or three days ([[paroxysmal attack]]s).<ref name="ECDC-Information-2024" /><ref name="Crutcher-1996" />

Symptoms typically begin 10–15 days after the initial mosquito bite, but can occur as late as several months after infection. Travellers taking preventative malaria medications may develop symptoms once they stop taking the drugs.<ref name="CDC-Features-2024">{{Cite web |date=20 March 2024 |title=Clinical Features of Malaria |url=https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/hcp/clinical-features/index.html |access-date=16 January 2026 |website=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention |language=en-us |archive-date=19 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260119021035/https://www.cdc.gov/malaria/hcp/clinical-features/index.html/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Severe malaria occurs when the Plasmodium infection causes damage to vital organs such as the kidney, liver, lungs or brain. Symptoms include severe [[anaemia]], jaundice, [[Convulsion|convulsions]], confusion, [[coma]], [[kidney failure]] and eventually death.<ref name="CDC-Features-2024" /><ref name="ECDC-Information-2024" /> Severe malaria is usually caused by ''[[Plasmodium falciparum|P.&nbsp;falciparum]]'';<ref name="Crutcher-1996" /> it should be treated as a medical emergency.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Severe malaria |url=https://www.mmv.org/malaria/symptoms-and-treatments/severe-malaria |access-date=21 January 2026 |website=Medicines for Malaria Venture |language=en |archive-date=7 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407170534/https://www.mmv.org/malaria/symptoms-and-treatments/severe-malaria |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Complications===
A unique feature of ''P.&nbsp;falciparum'' is its ability to generate adhesive proteins on the surface of infected red blood cells (RBC). Infected RBCs obstruct capillaries (causing [[Hypoxia (medicine)|hypoxia]]) and accumulate in vital organs, interfering with their function.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Autino |first1=Beatrice |last2=Corbett |first2=Yolanda |last3=Castelli |first3=Francesco |last4=Taramelli |first4=Donatella |title=Pathogenesis of Malaria in Tissues and Blood |journal=Mediterranean Journal of Hematology and Infectious Diseases |date=4 October 2012 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=e2012061 |doi=10.4084/mjhid.2012.061 |pmc=3499994 |pmid=23170190}}</ref> ''P.&nbsp;falciparum'' infection underlies most severe complications of malaria.<ref name="WHO-Factsheet-2025" />

Cerebral malaria is a form of severe malaria affecting the brain. Infected RBCs blocking capillaries in the brain trigger an immune reaction, which in turn damages the [[Blood–brain barrier|blood-brain barrier]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schiess |first1=Nicoline |last2=Villabona-Rueda |first2=Andres |last3=Cottier |first3=Karissa E. |last4=Huether |first4=Katherine |last5=Chipeta |first5=James |last6=Stins |first6=Monique F. |title=Pathophysiology and neurologic sequelae of cerebral malaria |journal=Malaria Journal |date=December 2020 |volume=19 |issue=1 |article-number=266 |doi=10.1186/s12936-020-03336-z |doi-access=free |pmc=7376930 |pmid=32703204}}</ref> Individuals with cerebral malaria exhibit [[neurological disorder|neurological]] symptoms, such as confusion, [[seizure]]s, or [[coma]].<ref name="Bartoloni-2012" /> Cerebral malaria, if untreated, can lead to death within forty-eight hours of the first symptoms; survivors may have long-term neurological damage.<ref name="Bartoloni-2012" /><ref name="ECDC-Information-2024" />
