===1 January===
[[File:COVID-19-outbreak-timeline.gif|thumb|Animated map of confirmed COVID-19 cases from 12 January to 29 February 2020.]]
[[File:COVID-19 cases in China.svg|thumb|Date when first case in each first-level administration was reported.]]

[[Xinhua News]] reported that the [[Huanan Seafood Market]] was closed on 1 January 2020 for cleaning and disinfection.<ref name = "XinhuaJan1">{{cite news |title=8人因网上散布"武汉病毒性肺炎"不实信息被依法处理 [8 Legally Sanctioned for Spreading False Information on the 'Wuhan Viral Pneumonia' Online] |url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/2020-01/01/c_1125412773.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126113852/http://www.xinhuanet.com/2020-01/01/c_1125412773.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 January 2020 |access-date=19 May 2020 |agency=Xinhua News Agency |date=1 January 2020 |language=zh |quote=2020年1月1日，华南海鲜批发市场已休市整治 [On 1 January 2020, the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market closed for remediation.]}}</ref><ref name="promedmail">{{Cite web |date=2020-01-02 |title=Undiagnosed pneumonia – China (HU) (01): wildlife sales, market closed, RFI Archive Number: 20200102.6866757 |url=https://promedmail.org/promed-post/?id=6866757 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414011106/https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/kleelerner/files/20200102_promed_-undiagnosed_pneumonia_-_china_hubei_01-_wildlife_sales_market_closed_request_for_information.pdf |archive-date=2021-04-14 |archive-format=[[Internet Archive]] |access-date=13 January 2020 |website=[[ProMED-mail]] |publisher=[[International Society for Infectious Diseases]] |via=[[Harvard]] OpenScholar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1 January 2020 |title=China investigating outbreak of respiratory illness |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/china-pneumonia-outbreak-1.5412327 |access-date=May 18, 2021 |work=[[CBC.ca]] |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |agency=[[The Associated Press]]}}</ref>

US CDC Director [[Robert R. Redfield|Robert Redfield]] was briefed about the severity of the virus from his Chinese counterpart [[George F. Gao]] when he was on vacation with his family—according to reports, what he heard "rattled him".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weiland |first=Noah |date=4 April 2020 |title=The Lost Month: How a Failure to Test Blinded the U.S. to Covid-19 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/28/us/testing-coronavirus-pandemic.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007090140/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/28/us/testing-coronavirus-pandemic.html |archive-date=2024-10-07 |access-date=10 April 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

The WHO Newsroom stated that "the causal agent has not yet been identified or confirmed", and noted it had requested further information from the Chinese authorities to assess the risk.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=2020-01-05 |title=Pneumonia of unknown cause – China |url=https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2020-DON229 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009200502/https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2020-DON229 |archive-date=2024-10-09 |access-date=2024-11-12 |website=[[World Health Organization]]}}</ref>

===2 January===
A later, February study of patients admitted to the hospital in Wuhan between 16 December 2019 and 2 January 2020 was able to identify, during this time period, a total of 41 patients had contracted the novel coronavirus, 27 (66%) with direct exposure to Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market.<ref name="auto1">{{cite journal|url= |title=Clinical features of patients infected with 2019 novel coronavirus in Wuhan, China|first1=Chaolin|last1=Huang|first2=Yeming|last2=Wang|first3=Xingwang|last3=Li|first4=Lili|last4=Ren|first5=Jianping|last5=Zhao|first6=Yi|last6=Hu|first7=Li|last7=Zhang|first8=Guohui|last8=Fan|first9=Jiuyang|last9=Xu|first10=Xiaoying|last10=Gu|first11=Zhenshun|last11=Cheng|first12=Ting|last12=Yu|first13=Jiaan|last13=Xia|first14=Yuan|last14=Wei|first15=Wenjuan|last15=Wu|first16=Xuelei|last16=Xie|first17=Wen|last17=Yin|first18=Hui|last18=Li|first19=Min|last19=Liu|first20=Yan|last20=Xiao|first21=Hong|last21=Gao|first22=Li|last22=Guo|first23=Jungang|last23=Xie|first24=Guangfa|last24=Wang|first25=Rongmeng|last25=Jiang|first26=Zhancheng|last26=Gao|first27=Qi|last27=Jin|first28=Jianwei|last28=Wang|first29=Bin|last29=Cao|date=24 January 2020|journal=The Lancet|volume=395|issue=10223|pages=497–506|doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30183-5|pmid=31986264|pmc=7159299|doi-access=free}}</ref> All 41 patients were subsequently relocated from the hospital they had originally been diagnosed in to the Jinyintan Hospital in Wuhan, China.<ref name="auto1"/> WHO declared that its three concerned levels (China country office, Regional Office for the Western Pacific and headquarters) have been working together to respond to the outbreak.{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}

===3 January===
The Chinese government formally notified the US of the outbreak. At a White House briefing in 20 March, Health and Human Services Secretary [[Alex Azar]] said officials had been alerted to the initial reports of the virus by discussions between CDC director [[Robert R. Redfield Jr.|Robert Redfield]] and Chinese CDC Director Gao on 3 January. Mr. Azar also told his chief of staff to make sure that the National Security Council was aware that "this (the outbreak) is a very big deal".<ref>C-Span. (20 March 2020). White House Coronavirus News Conference. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vy1_K76Vjdc YouTube website] approx. 1 hour 2 minutes in. Retrieved 20 March 2020.</ref><ref name=":11">{{cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Shane |last2=Miller |first2=Greg |last3=Dawsey |first3=Josh |last4=Nakashima |first4=Ellen |title=U.S. intelligence reports from January and February warned about a likely pandemic |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/us-intelligence-reports-from-january-and-february-warned-about-a-likely-pandemic/2020/03/20/299d8cda-6ad5-11ea-b5f1-a5a804158597_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=13 April 2020  |date=20 March 2020}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last1=Shear|first1=Michael D.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/07/us/politics/trump-coronavirus.html|title=Inside Trump Administration, Debate Raged Over What to Tell Public|date=7 March 2020|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=14 April 2020|last2=Fink|first2=Sheri|issn=0362-4331|last3=Weiland|first3=Noah}}</ref> The BBC ran its first story on the outbreak.<ref>{{cite news |title=China pneumonia outbreak: Mystery virus probed in Wuhan |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-50984025 |access-date=24 December 2020 |agency=BBC |date=3 January 2020}}</ref>

Health authorities in Wuhan reported 44 cases, a big jump from the 27 reported on Tuesday. Eleven of the 44 were seriously ill, the Wuhan Municipal Health Commission said, although there had been no reported deaths to date. The health of the 121 close contacts of the cases was being monitored.<ref name="BRANSWELL">{{cite web |last1=Branswell |first1=Helen |title=Experts parse limited information about mystery outbreak in China |url=https://www.statnews.com/2020/01/04/mystery-pneumonia-outbreak-china/ |website=STAT |access-date=8 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128223237/https://www.statnews.com/2020/01/04/mystery-pneumonia-outbreak-china/ |archive-date=28 January 2020 |date=4 January 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Chinese scientists at the National Institute of Viral Disease Control and Prevention (IVDC) ruled out the possibilities for 26 common respiratory pathogens, including influenza A and B virus, parainfluenza virus, adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus metapneumovirus rhinovirus, enterovirus, and other common respiratory viruses. They determined the genetic sequence of the novel β-genus coronaviruses (naming it '2019-nCoV') from specimens collected from patients in Wuhan, China, and three distinct strains were established.<ref name="2019-nCoV">{{cite journal |last2=Li |first2=Qun |author1=((The 2019-nCoV Outbreak Joint Field Epidemiology Investigation Team)) |title=An Outbreak of NCIP (2019-nCoV) Infection in China |journal=China CDC Weekly |date=1 January 2020 |volume=2 |issue=5 |pages=79–80 |url=http://weekly.chinacdc.cn/en/article/id/e3c63ca9-dedb-4fb6-9c1c-d057adb77b57 |location=Wuhan, Hubei Province  |doi=10.46234/ccdcw2020.022 |issn=2096-7071 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128152930/http://weekly.chinacdc.cn/en/article/id/e3c63ca9-dedb-4fb6-9c1c-d057adb77b57 |archive-date=28 January 2020 |url-status=live |access-date=8 February 2020 |via=weekly.chinacdc.cn|doi-access=free |pmid=34594812 |pmc=8393104}}</ref>

China's [[National Health Commission]] (NHC) ordered institutions to not publish any information that related to the disease, and ordered labs to either transfer all samples to designated testing institutions, or destroy them. The order did not list any designated testing institutions.<ref name=Straits>{{cite web |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/how-early-signs-of-the-coronavirus-were-spotted-spread-and-throttled-in-china?mod=article_inline |title=How early signs of the coronavirus were spotted, spread and throttled in China |last1=Yu |first1=Gao |last2=Yanfeng |first2=Peng |last3=Rui |first3=Yang |last4=Yuding |first4=Feng |last5=Danmeng |first5=Ma |last6=Murphy |first6=Flynn |last7=Wei |first7=Han |last8=Shen |first8=Timmy |date=February 28, 2020 |website=The Straits Times |publisher=Singapore Press Holdings |access-date=November 22, 2020 |quote="Then on Jan 3, China's National Health Commission (NHC), the nation's top health authority, ordered institutions not to publish any information related to the unknown disease, and ordered labs to transfer any samples they had to designated testing institutions, or to destroy them. The order, which Caixin has seen, did not specify any designated testing institutions." |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426133851/https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/how-early-signs-of-the-coronavirus-were-spotted-spread-and-throttled-in-china?mod=article_inline |archive-date=26 April 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Li Wenliang]], a Wuhan ophthalmologist, was summoned to the Wuhan Public Security Bureau where he was told to sign an official confession and admonition letter promising to cease spreading "false" "rumors" regarding the coronavirus. In the letter, he was reprimanded for "making false comments by announcing the confirmation of 7 cases of SARS at the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market" that had "severely disturbed the social order". The letter stated, "We solemnly warn you: If you keep being stubborn, with such impertinence, and continue this illegal activity, you will be brought to justice—is that understood?" Li signed the confession writing: "Yes, I understand."<ref name="auto27">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51364382|title=The Chinese doctor who tried to warn about coronavirus|first=Stephanie|last=Hegarty|date=6 February 2020|work=BBC News|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206233545/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51364382|archive-date=6 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

===4 January===
The United Nations agency activated its incident-management system at the country, regional, and global level and was standing ready to launch a broader response if it was needed. The WHO's regional office in Manila said in Twitter posts Saturday: "#China has reported to WHO regarding a cluster of pneumonia cases in Wuhan, Hubei Province. The Govt has also met with our country office, and updated @WHO on the situation. Govt actions to control the incident have been instituted and investigations into the cause are ongoing."<ref name="auto29"/> The US CDC Director Redfield, following up the previous day's contact, emailed the Chinese CDC Director, Gao, formally offering to send US experts to China to investigate the outbreak.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kessler|first=Glenn|title=Analysis: Did Trump offer experts to China to help with the coronavirus?|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2020/04/03/how-much-pressure-did-trump-put-china-access-concerning-coronavirus/|access-date=2020-10-11|issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

The head of the University of Hong Kong's Center for Infection, Ho Pak-Leung, warned that the city should implement the strictest possible monitoring system for a mystery new viral pneumonia that infected dozens of people on the mainland, as it was highly possible that the illness was spreading from human to human. The microbiologist also warned that there could be a surge in cases during the upcoming Chinese New Year. Ho said he hoped the mainland would release more details as soon as possible about the patients infected with the disease, such as their medical history, to help experts analyze the illness and to allow for more effective preventive measures to be put in place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1500994-20200104.htm?|title=Wuhan virus probably is spreading between people|publisher=RTHK|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200105132418/https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1500994-20200104.htm|archive-date=5 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

The Singapore Ministry of Health said on Saturday, 4 January, that it had been notified of the first suspected case of the "mystery Wuhan virus" in Singapore, involving a three-year-old girl from China who had pneumonia and a travel history to the Chinese city of Wuhan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/wuhan-pneumonia-first-suspect-case-identified-here|title=Wuhan pneumonia: First suspected case reported in Singapore|date=4 January 2020|website=The Straits Times|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115062654/https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/wuhan-pneumonia-first-suspect-case-identified-here|archive-date=15 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 January, the Singapore Ministry of Health released a press statement stating that the earlier suspected case was not linked to the pneumonia cluster in Wuhan and was also tested negative for the SARS and MERS-CoV.<ref>{{cite web |title=Update On Local Situation Regarding Severe Pneumonia Cluster In Wuhan |url=https://www.moh.gov.sg/news-highlights/details/update-on-local-situation-regarding-severe-pneumonia-cluster-in-wuhan-5-jan |website=MOH |access-date=18 March 2020 |date=5 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309183047/https://www.moh.gov.sg/news-highlights/details/update-on-local-situation-regarding-severe-pneumonia-cluster-in-wuhan-5-jan |archive-date=9 March 2020 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 4 January, journalist Helen Branswell wrote that, while social media platforms suggested that China was not being transparent about the outbreak, scientists disagreed. Virologist Ralph Baric commented, "They have many of the best virologists in the world there that are working on this."<ref name="BRANSWELL"/><ref name="auto29">{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-01-04/china-pneumonia-outbreak-spurs-who-action-as-mystery-lingers|title=China Pneumonia Outbreak Spurs WHO Action as Mystery Lingers|date=4 January 2020|website=[[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]]|first=Jason|last=Gale|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114204434/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-01-04/china-pneumonia-outbreak-spurs-who-action-as-mystery-lingers|archive-date=14 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

===5 January===
The number of suspected cases reached 59 with seven in a critical condition. All were quarantined and local medical officials commenced the monitoring of 163 of their contacts. At this time, there had been no reported cases of human-to-human transmission or presentations in healthcare workers.<ref name="Schnirring6Jan20">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/questions-still-swirl-over-chinas-unexplained-pneumonia-outbreak|title=Questions still swirl over China's unexplained pneumonia outbreak|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=6 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200106222635/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/questions-still-swirl-over-chinas-unexplained-pneumonia-outbreak|archive-date=6 January 2020|access-date=7 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="5 Jan">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51000910|title=China pneumonia: Sars ruled out as dozens fall ill in Wuhan|date=5 January 2020|access-date=6 January 2020|website=BBC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200106005035/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51000910|archive-date=6 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Zhang Yong-Zhen]], a virologist at Fudan University, deposits the second known complete genome (Wuhan-Hu-1) in sequence database [[GenBank]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2020-01-12 |title=Wuhan seafood market pneumonia virus isolate Wuhan-Hu-1, complete genome, GenBank: MN908947.1 |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/MN908947.1 |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=Genbank}}</ref> The sequence record was initially embargoed and thus not visible to the public.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dispute simmers over who first shared SARS-CoV-2's genome |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/dispute-simmers-over-who-first-shared-sars-cov-2-s-genome |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=www.science.org}}</ref>

Early investigations into the cause of the pneumonia ruled out [[seasonal influenza|seasonal flu]], SARS, [[Middle East respiratory syndrome|MERS]], and [[avian flu|bird flu]].<ref name="Hui14Jan2020">{{cite journal|last1=Hui|first1=David S.|last2=Azhar|first2=Esam EI|last3=Madani|first3=Tariq A.|last4=Ntoumi|first4=Francine|last5=Kock|first5=Richard|last6=Dar|first6=Osman|last7=Ippolito|first7=Giuseppe|last8=Mchugh|first8=Timothy D.|last9=Memish|first9=Ziad A.|last10=Drosten|first10=Christian|last11=Zumla|first11=Alimuddin|date=14 January 2020|title=The continuing epidemic threat of novel coronaviruses to global health – the latest novel coronavirus outbreak in Wuhan, China|url=https://www.ijidonline.com/article/S1201-9712(20)30011-4/pdf|url-status=live|journal=International Journal of Infectious Diseasesglish|volume=91|pages=264–266|doi=10.1016/j.ijid.2020.01.009|issn=1201-9712|pmid=31953166|pmc=7128332|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131005858/https://www.ijidonline.com/article/S1201-9712(20)30011-4/pdf|archive-date=31 January 2020|access-date=8 February 2020|author-link10=Christian Drosten}}</ref><ref name="CDC6Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/watch/pneumonia-china|title=Pneumonia of Unknown Cause in China – Watch – Level 1, Practice Usual Precautions – Travel Health Notices {{!}} Travelers' Health {{!}} CDC|date=6 January 2020|website=wwwnc.cdc.gov|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108143634/https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/watch/pneumonia-china|archive-date=8 January 2020|access-date=7 January 2020}}</ref>

''Disease Outbreak News'' was WHO's first international media report summarizing details of the Wuhan outbreak.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2020-DON229 |title=Pneumonia of unknown cause – China |work=Disease Outbreak News |publisher=WHO |date=5 January 2020 |access-date=25 August 2021}}</ref>

===6 January===
On Monday, 6 January, the Wuhan health authorities announced they continued seeking the cause but had so far ruled out influenza, avian influenza, adenovirus, and coronaviruses SARS and MERS as the respiratory pathogen that had infected 59 people as of 5 January.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.axios.com/china-pneumonia-oubtreak-wuhan-e2ef8914-6bd7-46db-814d-1609d590ee07.html|title=China hunts cause of mysterious pneumonia outbreak in Wuhan|first=Eileen Drage|last=O'Reilly|website=Axios|date=6 January 2020 |access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107094738/https://www.axios.com/china-pneumonia-oubtreak-wuhan-e2ef8914-6bd7-46db-814d-1609d590ee07.html|archive-date=7 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The ''New York Times'' ran its first story on the outbreak.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wee |first1=Sui-Lee |last2=Wang |first2=Vivian |title=China Grapples With Mystery Pneumonia-Like Illness |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/06/world/asia/china-SARS-pneumonialike.html |access-date=24 December 2020 |agency=The New York Times |date=6 January 2020}}</ref>

===7 January===
Scientists of the National Institute of Viral Disease Control and Prevention (IVDC) confirmed the novel coronavirus isolated on 3 January was the pathogenic cause of the viral pneumonia of unknown etiology (VPUE) cluster, and designated the disease as a novel coronavirus-infected pneumonia (NCIP).<ref name="2019-nCoV" /> Scientists in China announced the discovery of a new coronavirus.<ref>{{Citation|title=Pneumonia cases in China's Wuhan could be due to new type of virus: WHO| date=8 January 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jggndUgvhrk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126024842/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jggndUgvhrk|access-date=7 February 2020|archive-date=26 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/new-virus-discovered-by-chinese-scientists-investigating-pneumonia-outbreak-11578485668|title=New Virus Discovered by Chinese Scientists Investigating Pneumonia Outbreak|last=Khan|first=Natasha|date=9 January 2020|work=The Wall Street Journal|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202154104/https://www.wsj.com/articles/new-virus-discovered-by-chinese-scientists-investigating-pneumonia-outbreak-11578485668|archive-date=2 February 2020|access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

In a closed meeting of the [[Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party]], [[Xi Jinping]] "made requests for the prevention and control work of the coronavirus outbreak" and issued instructions to similar ends. This meeting occurred 13 days before Xi's first public comments on the outbreak on 20 January.<ref>{{cite news |title=Highlights: China's Xi recounts early role in coronavirus battle |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-xi-highlights/highlights-chinas-xi-recounts-early-role-in-coronavirus-battle-idUSKBN20B1MC |access-date=19 May 2020 |work=Reuters |date=17 February 2020}}</ref>

Since the outburst of social media discussion of the mysterious pneumonia outbreak in Wuhan, China, Chinese authorities censored the hashtag #WuhanSARS and were now investigating anyone who was allegedly spreading misleading information about the outbreak on social media.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lanese |first1=Nicoletta |title=A New, Unidentified Virus Is Causing Pneumonia Outbreak in China, Officials Say |url=https://www.livescience.com/china-mystery-pneumonia-is-not-sars.html |website=livescience.com |access-date=8 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115233549/https://www.livescience.com/china-mystery-pneumonia-is-not-sars.html |archive-date=15 January 2020  |date=7 January 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) created an "incident management system" and issued a travel notice Monday for travellers to Wuhan, Hubei province, China due to the cluster of cases of pneumonia of an unknown etiology".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kff.org/news-summary/chinese-health-authorities-work-to-discover-cause-of-viral-pneumonia-outbreak-cdc-issues-travel-notice-for-wuhan/|title=Chinese Health Authorities Work To Discover Cause Of Viral Pneumonia Outbreak; CDC Issues Travel Notice For Wuhan|date=7 January 2020}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite news|last1=Shear|first1=Michael D.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/28/us/testing-coronavirus-pandemic.html|title=The Lost Month: How a Failure to Test Blinded the U.S. to Covid-19|date=28 March 2020|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=13 April 2020|last2=Goodnough|first2=Abby|issn=0362-4331|last3=Kaplan|first3=Sheila|last4=Fink|first4=Sheri|last5=Thomas|first5=Katie|last6=Weiland|first6=Noah}}</ref>

===8 January===
South Korea authorities put a 36-year-old Chinese woman under isolated treatment amid concerns that she had brought back a form of viral pneumonia that had sickened dozens in mainland China and Hong Kong in the previous weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/30c5bf016c52748eebc6371fe3b17321|title=South Korea reports 1st possible case of viral pneumonia|date=8 January 2020|website=AP News|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110163726/https://apnews.com/30c5bf016c52748eebc6371fe3b17321|archive-date=10 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The unidentified woman, who worked for a South Korean company near capital Seoul, had experienced cough and fever since returning from a five-day trip to China on 30 December, the KCDC said in a press release. The woman had spent time in Wuhan, China, but had not visited the Huanan Seafood Market.{{citation needed|date=April 2020}}

===9 January===
==== First reported death ==== 
The first death from the virus occurred in a 61-year-old man who was a regular customer at the market. He had several significant medical conditions, including chronic liver disease, and died from heart failure and pneumonia. The incident was reported in China by the [[National Health Commission|health commission]] via [[Chinese state media]] on 11 January.<ref name="Schnirring11Jan2020">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/china-releases-genetic-data-new-coronavirus-now-deadly|title=China releases genetic data on new coronavirus, now deadly|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=11 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111215102/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/china-releases-genetic-data-new-coronavirus-now-deadly|archive-date=11 January 2020|access-date=12 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="QinNYT11Jan2020">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/10/world/asia/china-virus-wuhan-death.html|title=China Reports First Death From New Virus|last1=Qin|first1=Amy|date=10 January 2020|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=11 January 2020|url-status=live|last2=Hernández|first2=Javier name="ECDP14Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/news-events/update-cluster-pneumonia-cases-associated-novel-coronavirus-wuhan-china-2019| title=Update: Cluster of pneumonia cases January 2020|access-date=18 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="Strait11Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-reports-first-death-in-wuhan-pneumonia-outbreak|title=China 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

The WHO confirmed that the novel coronavirus had been isolated from one person who had been hospitalized.<ref name=Schnirring9Jan2020/><ref name="WHO9Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.who.int/china/news/detail/09-01-2020-who-statement-regarding-cluster-of-pneumonia-cases-in-wuhan-china|title=WHO Statement Regarding Cluster of Pneumonia Cases in Wuhan, China|location=China|date=9 January 2020 |publisher=World Health Organization|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114133102/https://www.who.int/china/news/detail/09-01-2020-who-statement-regarding-cluster-of-pneumonia-cases-in-wuhan-china|archive-date=14 January 2020|access-date=9 January 2020}}</ref> On the same day, the [[European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control]] posted its first risk assessment.<ref name="Schnirring10Jan2020">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/pressure-builds-china-share-info-new-coronavirus|title=Pressure builds on China to share info on new coronavirus|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=10 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110230138/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/pressure-builds-china-share-info-new-coronavirus|archive-date=10 January 2020|access-date=11 January 2020}}</ref> The WHO also reported that Chinese authorities had acted swiftly,<ref name=Schnirring9Jan2020>{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/more-details-emerge-new-coronavirus-wuhan-cluster|title=More details emerge on new coronavirus in Wuhan cluster|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=9 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110062152/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/more-details-emerge-new-coronavirus-wuhan-cluster|archive-date=10 January 2020|access-date=9 January 2020}}</ref> identifying the novel coronavirus within weeks of the onset of the outbreak, with the total number of positively tested people being 41.<ref name="Lucey">{{cite web|url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2020/01/14/china-response-wuhan-pneumonia-better-sars/|title=China Deserves Some Credit for Its Handling of the Wuhan Pneumonia|last1=Lucey|first1=Daniel|author-link=Daniel R. Lucey|last2=Sparrow|first2=Annie|date=14 January 2020|website=Foreign Policy|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115042408/https://foreignpolicy.com/2020/01/14/china-response-wuhan-pneumonia-better-sars/|archive-date=15 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref>

Chinese scientists reported on Chinese state broadcaster CCTV that they had found a new "coronavirus in 15 of 57 patients with the illness in the central city of Wuhan, saying it has been preliminarily identified as the pathogen for the outbreak".<ref name="auto25">{{cite web|url=https://thethaiger.com/hot-news/tourism/chinese-scientists-identify-the-wuhan-virus-screening-continues-on-thai-bound-flights|title=Chinese scientists identify the 'Wuhan Virus'. Screening continues on Thai-bound flights.|date=9 January 2020|website=The Thaiger|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110134224/https://thethaiger.com/hot-news/tourism/chinese-scientists-identify-the-wuhan-virus-screening-continues-on-thai-bound-flights|archive-date=10 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The scientists announced that the current 'Wuhan Virus', a coronavirus, appears to not be as lethal as SARS. They reported that the new viral outbreak was first detected in the city of Wuhan on 12 December 2019.<ref name="auto25"/> Additionally, a total of 59 people have been identified as contracting the illness, seven patients had been in a critical condition at some stage, and no healthcare workers were reported as having been infected.<ref name="auto25"/>

===10 January===
====Genome sequence becomes public====
The genome of the isolated 2019-nCoV, a virus from the same family as the SARS coronavirus, was posted on [[Virological.org]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-11 |title=Novel 2019 coronavirus genome |url=https://virological.org/t/novel-2019-coronavirus-genome/319 |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=Virological}}</ref> by [[Edward C. Holmes|Edward Holmes]] on behalf of Zhang Yong-Zhen of Fudan University, Shanghai.<ref name="Schnirring11Jan2020" /><ref name="Schnirring13Jan2020">{{cite web |last=Schnirring |first=Lisa |date=13 January 2020 |title=Thailand finds Wuhan novel coronavirus in traveler from China |url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/thailand-finds-wuhan-novel-coronavirus-traveler-china |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113231747/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/thailand-finds-wuhan-novel-coronavirus-traveler-china |archive-date=13 January 2020 |access-date=14 January 2020 |website=CIDRAP}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The sequence had already been uploaded to [[GenBank]] on 5 January 2020, but was embargoed and thus not available to the public. Shortly thereafter, three genetic sequences of the isolated novel coronavirus from the [[Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention]], one from the [[Peking Union Medical College|Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences]], and one from [[Wuhan Jinyintan Hospital]] were posted to [[GISAID]].<ref name="Schnirring13Jan2020"/>

On 10 January 2020, Li Wenliang, Chinese ophthalmologist and coronavirus whistleblower, started having symptoms of a dry cough. On 12 January 2020, Wenliang started having a fever. He was admitted to the hospital on 14 January 2020. His parents also contracted the coronavirus (presumably from Wenliang) and were admitted to the hospital with him. Wenliang tested negative several times for the coronavirus until finally testing positive on 30 January 2020.<ref name="auto27"/> He died on 7 February 2020.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Green |first1=Andrew |title=Li Wenliang |journal=The Lancet |date=18 February 2020 |volume=395 |issue=10225 |page=682 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30382-2 | pmc=7137172  |doi-access=free |issn=0140-6736}}</ref>

First two patients in [[Shenzhen]], Guangdong, China attend [[University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital]].<ref name="caixinshenzhen">{{cite news|url=http://www.caixin.com/2020-03-01/101522551.html|title=特稿 {{!}} 深圳"人传人"结论是如何得出的|language=zh|trans-title=Feature {{!}} How Shenzhen's "people-to-people" conclusion was reached|date=1 March 2020|work=Caixin}}</ref>

===11 January===
The first two patients in Shenzhen city transferred into a negative pressure room in Third People's Hospital of Shenzhen City due to matching lab test results, symptoms, and epidemiology and are being listed as suspected cases. The cases were not confirmed at the time, because requirement from the Chinese government at the time was that first case in each city needs to be submitted to provincial CDC, verified by national CDC, and then evaluated and confirmed by a specific diagnostic team in national CDC.<ref name="caixinshenzhen" />

===11–12 January===
In China, more than 700 close contacts of the 41 confirmed cases, including more than 400 healthcare workers, had been monitored, with no new cases reported in China since 5 January.<ref name=CDC6Jan2020/><ref name="Schnirring6Jan20" /><ref name=Schnirring11Jan2020/><ref name="Schnirring7Jan20">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/nations-step-screening-and-await-word-chinas-pneumonia-outbreak|title=Nations step up screening and await word on China's pneumonia outbreak|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=7 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107220738/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/nations-step-screening-and-await-word-chinas-pneumonia-outbreak|archive-date=7 January 2020|access-date=8 January 2020}}</ref> Respiratory wards in Wuhan hospitals began reaching capacity around 12 January, with some people being denied care.<ref name="Reuters2">{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |title='Painful lesson': how a military-style lockdown unfolded in Wuhan |last1=Cadell |first1=Cate |last2=Chen |first2=Yawen |date=April 8, 2020 |website=Reuters |access-date=January 3, 2021 |archive-date=January 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106000113/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |quote=Hospital respiratory wards began reaching capacity by around Jan 12, and some people were being turned away, a half dozen Wuhan residents told Reuters.}}</ref> The WHO published initial guidance on travel advice, testing in the laboratory, and medical investigation.<ref name=Schnirring11Jan2020/> The WHO said that "The [Chinese] government reports that there is no clear evidence that the virus passes easily from person to person".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-01-29/coronavirus-timeline-from-wuhan-china-to-global-crisis/11903298 |title=From Wuhan to Australia: A timeline of key events in the spread of the deadly coronavirus |publisher=ABC News (Australian Broadcasting Corporation) |date=29 January 2020 |access-date=9 April 2020}}</ref>

===13 January===
The US [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] announced that the genome had been posted on the [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] genetic sequence database, [[GenBank]].<ref name=CDC13Jan2020>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/novel-coronavirus-2019.html|title=Novel Coronavirus 2019 {{!}} CDC|date=13 January 2020|website=www.cdc.gov|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114084712/https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/novel-coronavirus-2019.html|archive-date=14 January 2020|access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref> On the same day, Thailand witnessed the first confirmed case of 2019-nCoV, the first outside China.<ref name="WHO14Jan2010">{{cite web|url=https://www.who.int/csr/don/14-january-2020-novel-coronavirus-thailand-ex-china/en/|title=WHO {{!}} Novel Coronavirus – Thailand (ex-China)|date=14 January 2020|website=WHO|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121030737/https://www.who.int/csr/don/14-january-2020-novel-coronavirus-thailand-ex-china/en/|archive-date=21 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref> The affected 61-year-old Chinese woman, who was a resident of Wuhan, had not visited the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market, but was noted to have been to other markets. She had arrived in Bangkok on 8 January.<ref name="Schnirring14Jan2020">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/report-thailands-coronavirus-patient-didnt-visit-outbreak-market|title=Report: Thailand's coronavirus patient didn't visit outbreak market|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=14 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114230152/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/report-thailands-coronavirus-patient-didnt-visit-outbreak-market|archive-date=14 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref><ref>Li Yang Hsu, Po Ying Chia, and Jeremy FY Lim. (January 2020). "Opinion:The Novel Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) Epidemic". [http://www.annals.edu.sg/pdf/special/01ED20051_HsuLY_1.pdf Annals of the Academy of Medicine, Singapore website] 4, pp. 1–3.. Retrieved 25 March 2020.</ref> In response, the WHO urged China to continue searching for the source of the new virus.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-13|title=UN health agency urges China to continue search for source of new virus, as Thailand case emerges|url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2020/01/1055212|access-date=2020-08-03|website=UN News}}</ref>

===14 January===
WHO sent a tweet which stated, "preliminary investigations conducted by the Chinese authorities have found no clear evidence of human-to-human transmission of the novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV) identified in Wuhan, China".<ref>{{cite tweet |user=WHO |number=1217043229427761152 |date=14 January 2020 |title=Preliminary investigations conducted by the Chinese authorities have found no clear evidence of human-to-human transmission of the novel coronavirus... |access-date=10 April 2020}}</ref> According to Reuters in Geneva, WHO said there may have been limited human-to-human transmission of a new coronavirus in China within families, and it was possible there could be a wider outbreak.<ref name=":13">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-pneumonia-who-idUSKBN1ZD16J|title=WHO says new China coronavirus could spread, warns hospitals worldwide|date=14 January 2020|work=Reuters|access-date=22 April 2020}}</ref>

The Wuhan Municipal Health Committee published a Q&A regarding the coronavirus, stating: "current investigation hasn't found clear evidence of human to human transmission, however, the possibility of human to human transmission cannot be ruled out".<ref>{{cite web|title=新型冠状病毒感染的肺炎疫情知识问答 (14 January 2020 )|url=http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2019123108989 |language=zh|publisher=Wuhan Municipal Health Committee|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114173636/http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2020011509040|archive-date=14 January 2020}}</ref>

Two of the 41 confirmed cases in Wuhan were reported to include a married couple, raising the possibility of human-to-human transmission.<ref name="Schnirring14Jan2020" /><ref name="CDC15Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/novel-coronavirus-2019.html|title=Novel Coronavirus 2019 {{!}} CDC|date=15 January 2020|website=www.cdc.gov|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114084712/https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/novel-coronavirus-2019.html|archive-date=14 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020}}</ref>

[[Maria Van Kerkhove]], acting head of WHO's emerging diseases unit, said that there had been limited human-to-human transmission of the coronavirus, mainly small clusters in families, adding that "it is very clear right now that we have no sustained human-to-human transmission"<ref name=":13" /><ref>{{cite news|author=Sarah Newey |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/global-health/science-and-disease/refuses-rule-human-to-human-spread-chinas-mystery-virus-outbreak/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/global-health/science-and-disease/refuses-rule-human-to-human-spread-chinas-mystery-virus-outbreak/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=WHO refuses to rule out human-to-human spread in China's mystery coronavirus outbreak |newspaper=The Telegraph |date=14 January 2020 |access-date=30 March 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/wuhan-virus-has-limited-human-to-human-transmission-but-could-spread-wider-who |title=Wuhan virus has limited human-to-human transmission but could spread wider: WHO, East Asia News & Top Stories |work=The Straits Times |date=14 January 2020 |access-date=30 March 2020}}</ref>

Under 'Disease Outbreak News', in an article titled 'Novel Coronavirus – Thailand (ex-China)', WHO advised: 'No additional cases have been detected since 3 January 2020 in China.'<ref>{{Cite web |title=Novel Coronavirus – Thailand |url=https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2020-DON234 |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=www.who.int}}</ref>

In a confidential government teleconference on 15 January, between Ma Xiaowei, the head of the [[National Health Commission]] and the provincial health authorities, the government internally acknowledged the threat of a pandemic due to the reporting of the Thailand viral infection a day earlier and the public health threat that New Year holiday travel presented for the further spread of the virus.<ref>The Associated Press. (15 April 2020). "China didn't warn public of likely pandemic for 6 key days". [https://apnews.com/68a9e1b91de4ffc166acd6012d82c2f9 AP website] Retrieved 5 April 2020.</ref>

===15 January===
A second death occurred in a 69-year-old man in China on 15 January.<ref name="Schirring16Jan2020">{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/japan-has-1st-novel-coronavirus-case-china-reports-another-death|title=Japan has 1st novel coronavirus case; China reports another death|last=Schirring|first=Lisa|date=16 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120043657/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/japan-has-1st-novel-coronavirus-case-china-reports-another-death|archive-date=20 January 2020|access-date=16 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="Reuters16Jan2020">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-pneumonia-idUSKBN1ZG01B|title=China says second person dies in Wuhan pneumonia outbreak|date=17 January 2020|work=Reuters|access-date=17 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117105016/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-pneumonia-idUSKBN1ZG01B|archive-date=17 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

The first known travel-related case of 2019 novel coronavirus entered the United States: "The patient from Washington with confirmed 2019-nCoV infection returned to the United States from Wuhan on January 15, 2020. The patient sought care at a medical facility in the state of Washington, where the patient was treated for the illness. Based on the patient's travel history and symptoms, healthcare professionals suspected this new coronavirus. A clinical specimen was collected and sent to CDC overnight, where laboratory testing yesterday confirmed the diagnosis via CDC's Real-time Reverse Transcription-Polymerase Chain Reaction (rRT-PCR) test."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/media/releases/2020/p0121-novel-coronavirus-travel-case.html |title=First Travel-related Case of 2019 Novel Coronavirus Detected in United States {{pipe}} CDC |publisher=Cdc.gov |date=21 January 2020|access-date=4 April 2020}}</ref>

The US embassy in China issued a Health Alert Watch Level 1 for an outbreak of pneumonia in Wuhan, preliminarily identified to be caused by a novel coronavirus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://china.usembassy-china.org.cn/health-alert-update-novel-coronavirus-in-china/ |title=Health Alert Update – Novel Coronavirus in China  |publisher=U.S. Embassy & Consulates in China |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=10 April 2020}}</ref>

===16 January===
Researchers from the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) at [[Charité]]—Universitätsmedizin Berlin developed a new laboratory assay to detect the novel coronavirus. The assay protocol has been published by the WHO as a guideline for diagnostic detection for 2019-nCoV. The new assay enables suspected cases to be tested quickly.<ref name="DZIF20200116">{{cite web|url=https://www.dzif.de/en/researchers-develop-first-diagnostic-test-novel-coronavirus-china|title=Researchers develop first diagnostic test for novel coronavirus in China|date=16 January 2020|website=German Center for Infection Research (DZIF)}}</ref><ref name="Schirring16Jan2020" />

The WHO was alerted by Japan's [[Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare]] that the first case in Japan, a 30-year-old male Chinese national had tested positive to 2019-nCoV during a hospital stay between 10 and 15 January. He had not visited the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market, but possibly had close contact with an affected person in Wuhan.<ref name="Walter16Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japan-confirms-first-case-of-infection-with-new-china-coronavirus|title=Japan confirms first case of infection from Wuhan coronavirus; Vietnam quarantines two tourists|last=Walter|first=Sim|date=16 January 2020|website=The Straits Times|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116072051/https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japan-confirms-first-case-of-infection-with-new-china-coronavirus|archive-date=16 January 2020|access-date=16 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="WHO=16Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.who.int/csr/don/16-january-2020-novel-coronavirus-japan-ex-china/en/|title=Novel Coronavirus – Japan (ex-China)|publisher=World Health Organization|access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref>

Despite these developments, up until at least 16 January, Wuhan officials stated there had been no new cases for about two weeks, and only minimal measures had been put in place to slow the spread of the disease.<ref name="Reuters3">{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |title='Painful lesson': how a military-style lockdown unfolded in Wuhan |last1=Cadell |first1=Cate |last2=Chen |first2=Yawen |date=April 8, 2020 |website=Reuters |access-date=January 3, 2021 |archive-date=January 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106000113/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |quote=But at least up to Jan. 16, Wuhan's government said that no new cases of the disease had occurred for about two weeks, and the city continued as normal. Diners packed restaurants, shoppers flocked to commercial districts, and travellers headed to train stations and airports for their Lunar New Year holidays. Minimal measures were put in place to take the temperatures of residents in public places, or encourage them to wear protective masks, residents said.}}</ref> This policy would not change until the arrival of an epidemiological team from Beijing on 18 January.<ref name="Reuters3" />

===17 January===
On 17 January, Thailand's second confirmed case was reported in a 74-year-old woman who arrived in Bangkok on a flight from Wuhan.<ref name="Wee17Jan2020">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/15/world/asia/coronavirus-japan-china.html|title=Japan and Thailand Confirm New Cases of Chinese Coronavirus|last=Wee|first=Sui-Lee|date=15 January 2020|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=17 January 2020|url-status=live|issn=0362-4331|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116234710/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/15/world/asia/coronavirus-japan-china.html|archive-date=16 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="GovHK17Jan2020">{{cite web|url=https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202001/17/P2020011700960.htm|title=CHP closely monitors additional confirmed case of infection of novel coronavirus in Thailand|date=17 January 2020|publisher=Government of Hong Kong|access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref> The number of laboratory-confirmed cases rose to 45 in China.<ref name=Schnirring17Jan2020>{{cite web|url=http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/thailand-notes-2nd-ncov-case-cdc-begins-airport-screening|title=As Thailand notes 2nd nCoV case, CDC begins airport screening|last=Schnirring|first=Lisa|date=17 January 2020|website=CIDRAP|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117222155/http://www.cidrap.umn.edu/news-perspective/2020/01/thailand-notes-2nd-ncov-case-cdc-begins-airport-screening|archive-date=17 January 2020|access-date=18 January 2020}}</ref>

[[Yang Xiaobo (Hubei politician)|Yang Xiaobo]], head of the Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, died of pneumonia caused by the virus on 17 January.<ref name="Radio Free Asia">{{cite web|last1=Qiao|first1=Long|last2=Sing|first2=Man|last3=Wong|first3=Siu-san|title=Airlines Cut Flights to China As Coronavirus Infections Spike|url=https://www.rfa.org/english/news/china/flights-01292020125033.html/|website=Radio Free Asia|access-date=1 February 2020|date=29 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131163208/https://www.rfa.org/english/news/china/flights-01292020125033.html|archive-date=31 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

US CDC dispatched 100 people to three American airports to screen travellers coming from Wuhan, China.<ref name=":1" />

===18 January===
An epidemiological team from Beijing led by renowned Chinese scientist [[Zhong Nanshan]] arrived in Wuhan and began an investigation into the epidemic.<ref name="Reuters3" /> Officials reported 17 additional laboratory-confirmed cases, three of which were in critical condition. This brought the number of laboratory-confirmed cases in China to 62. The patients' ages ranged from 30 to 79. Nineteen were discharged and eight remain critical.<ref name="France-Presse19Jan2020">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/19/coronavirus-china-reports-17-new-cases-of-sars-like-mystery-virus|title=Coronavirus: China reports 17 new cases of Sars-like mystery virus|agency=Agence France-Presse|date=19 January 2020|work=The Guardian|access-date=19 January 2020|url-status=live|issn=0261-3077|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120043700/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/19/coronavirus-china-reports-17-new-cases-of-sars-like-mystery-virus|archive-date=20 January 2020}}</ref>

Controversially, the Wuhan City government held an annual banquet in the Baibuting community celebrating the Chinese New Year, preparing food at ten different locations for 40 thousand families and likely contributing to the spread of the virus.<ref>{{cite web |author1=胡博阳 |title=武汉"万家宴"：他们的淡定让人没法淡定 |url=http://www.bjnews.com.cn/opinion/2020/01/21/677335.html |website=bjnews.com.cn |language=zh |date=21 January 2020}}</ref> On 21 January 2020 when Wuhan mayor Zhou Xianwang was asked on state television why this banquet was held even after the number of cases had risen to 312, he responded, "The reason why the Baibuting community continued to host the banquet this year was based on the previous judgment that the spread of the epidemic was limited between humans, so there was not enough warning."<ref name=FT18Feb>{{cite web |title=Coronavirus: the cost of China's public health cover-up |url=https://www.ft.com/content/fa83463a-4737-11ea-aeb3-955839e06441 |url-access=subscription |website=[[Financial Times]] |access-date=8 February 2020 |date=6 February 2020}}</ref>

US Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Alex Azar spoke to Trump on the phone about the virus, during which Trump interjected to ask when flavored vaping products would be back on the market.<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":1" />

===19 January===
On 19 January, the first confirmed cases were reported in China, outside Wuhan, one in the southern province of Guangdong and two in Beijing.<ref name=":Sina20Jan2020">{{cite news|url=https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2020-01-20/doc-iihnzahk5231837.shtml|language=zh-cn|script-title=zh:广东确诊1例新型冠状病毒感染的肺炎病例|date=20 January 2020|work=[[Sina Corp|Sina]] News}}</ref> Wuhan reported 136 additional laboratory-confirmed cases, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed cases in China to 201. A new death was also reported in Wuhan, bringing the total number of fatalities in China to three.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2020012009077|title=武汉市卫生健康委员会|website=wjw.wuhan.gov.cn|access-date=20 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120052215/http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2020012009077|archive-date=20 January 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="wuhan20Jan2020">{{cite news|title=China reports 136 more cases in two days|url=http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2020012009077|access-date=20 January 2020|agency=Wuhan Municipal Health Commission|date=20 January 2020|language=zh|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120052215/http://wjw.wuhan.gov.cn/front/web/showDetail/2020012009077|archive-date=20 January 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===20 January===
On 20 January, after two medical staff were infected in Guangdong, [[National Health Commission|China National Health Commission]] confirmed that the virus was human-to-human transmissible.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |last1=Kuo |first1=Lily |title=China confirms human-to-human transmission of coronavirus |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/20/coronavirus-spreads-to-beijing-as-china-confirms-new-cases |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=30 March 2020 |location=Beijing |date=21 January 2020}}</ref> The investigation team from China's National Health Commission confirmed for the first time that the coronavirus can be transmitted between humans.<ref name="auto15">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51185836|title=Warning against cover-up as China virus cases jump|date=21 January 2020|work=BBC News|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205221505/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51185836|archive-date=5 February 2020|access-date=8 February 2020}}</ref>

Scientists from the China CDC identified three different strains of the 2019-nCoV, confirming that the original Wuhan coronavirus had mutated into two additional strains.<ref name="auto18">{{Cite journal|url=http://weekly.chinacdc.cn/en/article/id/a3907201-f64f-4154-a19e-4253b453d10c|title=A Novel Coronavirus Genome Identified in a Cluster of Pneumonia Cases—Wuhan, China 2019–2020 |first1=Wenjie |last1=Tan |first2=Xiang |last2=Zhao |first3=Xuejun |last3=Ma |first4=Wenling |last4=Wang |first5=Peihua|last5=Niu|first6=Wenbo|last6=Xu|first7=George F.|last7=Gao|first8=Guizhen|last8=Wu|date=1 January 2020|journal=China CDC Weekly |volume=2 |issue=4 |pages=61–62 |doi=10.46234/ccdcw2020.017 |pmid=34594763 |pmc=8393069 |via=weekly.chinacdc.cn|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207013959/http://weekly.chinacdc.cn/en/article/id/a3907201-f64f-4154-a19e-4253b453d10c|archive-date=7 February 2020|url-status=live|doi-access=free}}</ref>

[[Chinese Communist Party]] [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party|general secretary]] ([[Paramount leader]]), [[Xi Jinping]] said "people's lives and health should be given top priority and the spread of the outbreak should be resolutely curbed."<ref name=":4" /> [[State Council of the People's Republic of China|State Council]] [[Premier of the People's Republic of China|premier]] [[Li Keqiang]] urged decisive and effective efforts to prevent and control the epidemic.<ref name="Premier urged2">{{cite web|url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202001/21/WS5e26556ca31012821727269c.html|title=Chinese premier stresses curbing viral pneumonia epidemic|date=21 January 2020|website=[[China Daily]]|agency=[[Xinhua News Agency]]|location=Beijing|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200122124640/https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202001/21/WS5e26556ca31012821727269c.html|archive-date=22 January 2020|access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref> First confirmed case reported in South Korea.<ref name="Yonhap20Jan">{{cite web|url=https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200120004500320|title=S. Korea reports 1st confirmed case of China coronavirus|last=박상수|date=20 January 2020|work=Yonhap News Agency|access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref> Beijing and Guangdong reported an additional three and thirteen laboratory-confirmed cases, respectively. Shanghai confirms its first case, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed cases in China to 218.<ref name="strait20jan">{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/wuhan-virus-cases-hit-217-in-china-as-president-xi-jinping-pledges-to-curb-outbreak|title=Wuhan virus: China announces more confirmed cases, including in Shanghai and Guangdong|date=20 January 2020|website=The Straits Times|access-date=20 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121165225/https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/wuhan-virus-cases-hit-217-in-china-as-president-xi-jinping-pledges-to-curb-outbreak|archive-date=21 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/china-coronavirus-kills-third-person-spreads-to-more-cities-11579494221|title=Coronavirus Is Spreading Quickly Across China as Confirmed Cases Triple|last=Cheng|first=Chao Deng and Jonathan|website=The Wall Street Journal|date=21 January 2020|access-date=21 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121040231/https://www.wsj.com/articles/china-coronavirus-kills-third-person-spreads-to-more-cities-11579494221|archive-date=21 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> At least two people had become infected while living hundreds of miles from Wuhan.<ref name=":100">{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/19/asia/china-coronavirus-spike-intl-hnk/index.html|title=China confirms new coronavirus can spread between humans|first1=Nectar|last1=Gan|first2=Yong|last2=Xiong|publisher=CNN|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120040258/https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/19/asia/china-coronavirus-spike-intl-hnk/index.html|archive-date=20 January 2020|access-date=20 January 2020|first3=Eliza|last3=Mackintosh}}</ref>

The United States and South Korea each reported their first confirmed case of the coronavirus to the World Health Organization on 20 January.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Taylor|first=Derrick Bryson|url=https://www.nytimes.com/article/coronavirus-timeline.html|title=A Timeline of the Coronavirus Pandemic|date=7 April 2020|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=10 April 2020|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":9" /> US CDC developed its own testing kit after China shared the genetic sequence on 10 January and deployed it to detect the first coronavirus case. The testing kit used three small genetic sequences instead of two used by Germany. The test kits were found to be defective because the third sequence, or "probe", gave inconclusive results.<ref name=":12" /> US National Institutes of Health has begun development of a vaccine for the coronavirus.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cohen|first=Elizabeth|title=Vaccine for new Chinese coronavirus in the works|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/20/health/coronavirus-nih-vaccine-development/index.html|access-date=2020-10-11|website=CNN|date=21 January 2020}}</ref>

Five attendees of an as-yet-unnamed private international sales company meeting of 109 attendees, 94 from overseas, held from 20 to 22 January at the Grand Hyatt Hotel, Singapore, were diagnosed with the coronavirus upon returning home: one from Malaysia, two from South Korea, and two from Singapore.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com.my/news/regional/2020/02/06/another-south-korean-at-singapore-work-conference-infected-with-coronavirus|title=Another South Korean at Singapore work conference infected with coronavirus {{pipe}} The Star Online|website=The Star|date=6 February 2020 |location=Malaysia|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206233527/https://www.thestar.com.my/news/regional/2020/02/06/another-south-korean-at-singapore-work-conference-infected-with-coronavirus|archive-date=6 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/coronavirus-two-new-local-infections-singapore-confirmed|title=Coronavirus: Two new local infections in Singapore confirmed|date=7 February 2020|website=The Edge Markets|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206225036/https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/coronavirus-two-new-local-infections-singapore-confirmed|archive-date=6 February 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> One of the attendees was from Wuhan, China. It was reported that the company held a buffet for their delegates. These four diagnoses were not reported until 5 February 2020.<ref name="auto21">{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-singapore-summit-idUSKBN2000C7|title=WHO probes Singapore meet linked to spread of virus|date=6 February 2020|work=Reuters|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206230749/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-singapore-summit-idUSKBN2000C7|archive-date=6 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The first laboratory-confirmed case in Singapore of an unrelated 67-year-old native of Wuhan was not reported until 23 January 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/singapore-confirms-first-case-of-wuhan-virus|title=Singapore confirms first case of Wuhan virus; second case likely|date=23 January 2020|website=The Straits Times|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124014101/https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/singapore-confirms-first-case-of-wuhan-virus|archive-date=24 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> These cases linked to the meeting were the first evidence that the Wuhan coronavirus had spread through human-to-human contact outside China, which the WHO has said was deeply concerning and could signal evidence of a much larger outbreak.<ref name="auto21" /> As of 5 February 2020, the sister of a Malaysian who attended the meeting had been infected and four more local staff in Singapore were confirmed as having virus symptoms.<ref name="auto21" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3049350/coronavirus-malaysia-confirms-first-case-human|title=Coronavirus: Malaysia confirms human transmission arising from Singapore meeting|date=6 February 2020|website=South China Morning Post|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206232256/https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3049350/coronavirus-malaysia-confirms-first-case-human|archive-date=6 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

===21 January===
A total of 291 cases have now been reported across major cities in China, including Beijing and Shanghai. However, most patients are in Wuhan, the central city of 11&nbsp;million at the heart of the outbreak.<ref name="auto15"/>

A report by the MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis at Imperial College London suggested there could be more than 1,700 infections. However, Gabriel Leung, the dean of medicine at the University of Hong Kong, put the figure closer to 1,300.<ref name="auto15"/>

After 300 confirmed diagnoses and 6 deaths, Chinese state media warned lower-level officials not to cover up the spread of a new coronavirus.<ref name="auto15"/> Officials declared that anyone who concealed new cases would "be nailed on the pillar of shame for eternity", the political body responsible for law and order said. The outbreak has revived memories of the SARS virus when the local Chinese officials initially withheld information about the SARS epidemic from the public and later vastly under-reported the number of people that had been infected, downplayed the risks, and failed to provide timely information that experts say could have saved lives. In its commentary published online on Tuesday, 21 January 2020, the Communist Party's Central Political and Legal Commission talked of China having learned a "painful lesson" from the SARS epidemic and called for the public to be kept informed. Deception, it warned, could "turn a controllable natural disaster into a man-made disaster".<ref name="auto15"/>

The Wuhan Municipal Health Commission reported at least 15 medical workers in Wuhan have also been infected with the virus, with one in a critical condition.<ref name="auto15"/>

===22 January===

Officials announced a quarantine of the greater Wuhan, China area to commence on 23 January 2020 at 10:00&nbsp;a.m. No traffic would be allowed in or out of the city.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=ChinaDaily |number=1220052882596286465 |date=22 January 2020 |title=Public transportation such as bus, subway, ferry and long-distance bus in Wuhan will be temporarily closed... |access-date=8 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201183636/https://twitter.com/ChinaDaily/status/1220052882596286465 |archive-date=1 February 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Zhou Xianwang, the mayor of Wuhan, admitted that his team had not released information about the virus in a "timely" manner, resulting in over 5&nbsp;million people traveling out of the city before Wuhan was placed in quarantine. Zhou cited "[[Chinese Communist Party|party]]-reporting mechanisms", indicating that Wuhan needed authorization from the central government before they could make any announcement regarding the virus.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pai |first1=Akshay |title=Wuhan mayor admits 'withholding' information about outbreak, scientists fear 100,000 have already been infected |url=https://meaww.com/wuhan-coronavirus-mayor-admits-withholding-information-about-deadly-outbreak-offers-to-resign |website=meaww.com |access-date=8 April 2020  |date=27 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Zheng |first1=Sarah |title=Wuhan mayor under pressure to resign over response to virus outbreak |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3047230/wuhan-mayor-under-pressure-resign-over-response-coronavirus |website=South China Morning Post |access-date=8 April 2020  |date=23 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="Reuters4">{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |title='Painful lesson': how a military-style lockdown unfolded in Wuhan |last1=Cadell |first1=Cate |last2=Chen |first2=Yawen |date=April 8, 2020 |website=Reuters |access-date=January 3, 2021 |archive-date=January 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210106000113/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-wuhan-scientists-i/painful-lesson-how-a-military-style-lockdown-unfolded-in-wuhan-idUSKBN21Q0KD |quote=Wuhan's mayor, Zhou Xianwang, who kept his job, made a frank admission in an interview with state media a few days later that party-reporting mechanisms had stifled early action.}}</ref>

The US embassy in China raised the Health Alert to level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://china.usembassy-china.org.cn/health-alert-update-novel-coronavirus-in-china-3/ |title=Health Alert Update – Novel Coronavirus in China-Level 2  |publisher=U.S. Embassy & Consulates in China |date=22 January 2020 |access-date=10 April 2020}}</ref> President Trump said during an interview at the Economic Forum in Switzerland that "It's one person coming in from China, and we have it under control. It's—going to be just fine."<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/01/22/davos-2020-cnbcs-full-interview-with-president-trump.html|title=Full interview: President Trump discusses trade, impeachment, Boeing and Elon Musk with CNBC in Davos|last=Calia|first=Mike|date=22 January 2020|publisher=CNBC|access-date=14 April 2020}}</ref>

The WHO Emergency Committee met in Geneva to consider whether the virus had reached the level of a [[Public Health Emergency of International Concern]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-22|title=UN health emergency committee to re-convene on global threat posed by China coronavirus|url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2020/01/1055821|access-date=2020-08-03|website=UN News}}</ref>

Additionally, all outbound trains and flights were halted.<ref name=":7">{{cite web|url=https://view.inews.qq.com/w/WXN2020012301001306?uid=&devid=A55D8C74-EEF2-420C-8182-21F1D43348CF&qimei=34ae00a5-9e85-4f82-9afa-3c7ccb6d36d5|title=直击武汉天河机场："封城"前有96架航班飞往全国|access-date=23 January 2020}}</ref> According to the Science magazine, the travel quarantine of Wuhan delayed the overall epidemic progression by only 3 to 5 days in mainland China, but had a more marked effect at the international scale, where case importations were reduced by nearly 80% until mid February.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chinazzi|first1=Matteo|last2=Davis|first2=Jessica T.|last3=Ajelli|first3=Marco|last4=Gioannini|first4=Corrado|last5=Litvinova|first5=Maria|last6=Merler|first6=Stefano|last7=Piontti|first7=Ana Pastore y|last8=Mu|first8=Kunpeng|last9=Rossi|first9=Luca|last10=Sun|first10=Kaiyuan|last11=Viboud|first11=Cécile|date=6 March 2020|title=The effect of travel restrictions on the spread of the 2019 novel coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak|journal=Science|volume=368|issue=6489|pages=395–400|doi=10.1126/science.aba9757|issn=0036-8075|pmid=32144116|pmc=7164386|bibcode=2020Sci...368..395C|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Based on the considerations of the WHO Emergency Committee, the WHO declared the virus to not yet be an official [[Public Health Emergency of International Concern|PHEIC]], but warned that it was an emergency in China.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-23|title=Coronavirus: 'An emergency in China, but not yet a global health emergency'|url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2020/01/1055891|access-date=2020-08-03|website=UN News}}</ref>

===24 January===
A report by Chinese doctors and scientists published in ''[[The Lancet]]'' medical journal was titled "Clinical features of patients infected with 2019 novel coronavirus in Wuhan, China". It indicated that people can be symptom-free for several days while the coronavirus is incubating, increasing the risk of contagious infection without forewarning signs. According to their data, 13 of the initial 41 cases of the novel coronavirus had no link with the wet market in Wuhan purported to be the origin of the disease, and the evidence taken as a whole indicated human transmission.<ref name="auto1" /> They strongly recommended [[personal protective equipment]] for health workers dealing with patients, stressed the need for testing for the virus, and because of its "pandemic potential" careful surveillance was essential. The significance of this was highlighted on 18 March by [[Richard Horton (editor)|Richard Horton]], editor-in-chief of ''The Lancet''.<ref name="Horton 2020">{{cite web | last=Horton | first=Richard |author-link=Richard Horton (editor) | title=Scientists have been sounding the alarm on coronavirus for months. Why did Britain fail to act? | website=The Guardian | date=18 March 2020 | url=http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2020/mar/18/coronavirus-uk-expert-advice-wrong | access-date=23 April 2020}}</ref>

One of the earlier studies on person-to-person transmission was published by Hong Kong doctors in ''[[The Lancet]]'' titled "A familial cluster of pneumonia associated with the 2019 novel coronavirus indicating person-to-person transmission: a study of a family cluster". In the "Evidence before this study", it declared that "we searched PubMed on Jan 13, 2020, with no starting date limitations, using the terms "family", "pneumonia", "Wuhan", "coronavirus", and "novel" for articles in English. Our search did not reveal any reports of novel coronavirus pneumonia in Wuhan before 2020. We only noted family clusters of pneumonia due to the novel severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) coronavirus in 2003, and Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus in 2012."<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chan|first1=Jasper Fuk-Woo|last2=Yuan|first2=Shuofeng|last3=Kok|first3=Kin-Hang|last4=To|first4=Kelvin Kai-Wang|last5=Chu|first5=Hin|last6=Yang|first6=Jin|last7=Xing|first7=Fanfan|last8=Liu|first8=Jieling|last9=Yip|first9=Cyril Chik-Yan|last10=Poon|first10=Rosana Wing-Shan|last11=Tsoi|first11=Hoi-Wah|date=15 February 2020|title=A familial cluster of pneumonia associated with the 2019 novel coronavirus indicating person-to-person transmission: a study of a family cluster|url= |journal=The Lancet|volume=395|issue=10223|pages=514–523|doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30154-9|issn=0140-6736|pmid=31986261|pmc=7159286|bibcode=2020Lanc..395..514C |doi-access=free}}</ref>

The United Nations' [[World Health Organization|WHO]] Director-General [[Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus|Tedros Ghebreyesus]] said he was on his way to Beijing to confer with Chinese officials and health experts about the coronavirus outbreak.<ref name="reuters26jan">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-who-idUSKBN1ZP0OG|title=WHO chief says he is on way to China to confer on virus, boost response|date=26 January 2020|work=Reuters|access-date=26 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126185333/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-who-idUSKBN1ZP0OG|archive-date=26 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

China started requiring nationwide use of monitoring stations for screening, identification, and immediate isolation of coronavirus-infected travelers, including at airports, railway stations, bus stations, and ports.<ref name="china_measures">{{cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.com/china-orders-nationwide-measures-detect-virus-flights-trains-090541811.html|title=China orders nationwide measures to detect virus on flights, trains, buses|publisher=Yahoo! News|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126235511/https://news.yahoo.com/china-orders-nationwide-measures-detect-virus-flights-trains-090541811.html|archive-date=26 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

A tentative clinical profile for the new coronavirus (2019-nCoV) was published by an assistant professor of population health science at the [[Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai]] in New York. The lethality of the virus is unknown; however, the death toll has now climbed to above three percent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2020/01/26/2019-ncov-china-epidemic-pandemic-the-wuhan-coronavirus-a-tentative-clinical-profile/|title=How China's Coronavirus Is Spreading—and How to Stop It|first=Annie|last=Sparrow|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131025848/https://foreignpolicy.com/2020/01/26/2019-ncov-china-epidemic-pandemic-the-wuhan-coronavirus-a-tentative-clinical-profile/|archive-date=31 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Wang Xianliang, a Hubei provincial government official, died of pneumonia caused by the virus.<ref name="Radio Free Asia"/>

===27 January===
'''WHO''' Situation Report 7:<ref>{{Citation|url=https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/coronaviruse/situation-reports/20200127-sitrep-7-2019--ncov.pdf?sfvrsn=98ef79f5_2|title=Novel Coronavirus(2019-nCoV) Situation Report – 7|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131215148/https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/coronaviruse/situation-reports/20200127-sitrep-7-2019--ncov.pdf?sfvrsn=98ef79f5_2|archive-date=31 January 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

Gabriel Leung, Dean of the University of Hong Kong medical school and one of the foremost world experts on SARS and viruses, gave a three-hour presentation published on YouTube wherein he made nowcasts and forecasts of the coronavirus. Using traditional scientific modeling techniques that predict the spread of viruses, Leung projected the true number of COVID-19 infections was likely 10 times more than the official reported numbers.<ref>{{Citation|title=Dr Gabriel Leung Dean of Medicine dire projection| date=27 January 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CwXMPsbxFfo|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201190644/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CwXMPsbxFfo|archive-date=1 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Leung estimated that there were between 44,000 and 100,000 infections in China as of 24 January 2020. He stated that draconian measures were needed to slow the progress of the virus but that these measures would have no effect in stopping the coronavirus pandemic. He projected that the number of infections would continue exponentially, peaking out in late April or May 2020. Leung predicted that, at the peak of the pandemic, there could be up to 100,000 new infections per day. Leung subsequently published an article in ''The Lancet'' nowcasting and forecasting the likely progression of the Wuhan coronavirus taking into consideration numerous variables.<ref>{{Cite journal|url= |title=Nowcasting and forecasting the potential domestic and international spread of the 2019-nCoV outbreak originating in Wuhan, China: a modelling study|first1=Joseph T.|last1=Wu|first2=Kathy|last2=Leung|first3=Gabriel M.|last3=Leung|date=31 January 2020|journal=The Lancet|volume=395|issue=10225|pages=689–697|doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(20)30260-9|pmid=32014114|pmc=7159271|bibcode=2020Lanc..395..689W |doi-access=free}}</ref> Zhou Xianwang, the mayor of Wuhan, said on a Chinese state television talkshow that rules imposed by Beijing limited what he could disclose about the threat posed by the Wuhan coronavirus as it unfolded, suggesting "the central government was partially responsible for a lack of transparency that has marred the response to the fast-expanding health crisis."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/chinas-premier-tours-virus-epicenter-as-anger-bubbles-at-crisis-response-11580109098|title=Wuhan Mayor Says Beijing Rules Partially Responsible for Lack of Transparency|first=Josh|last=Chin|date=28 January 2020|work=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=8 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207052922/https://www.wsj.com/articles/chinas-premier-tours-virus-epicenter-as-anger-bubbles-at-crisis-response-11580109098|archive-date=7 February 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>
